facts.claim: RULE (audio rate): never force a sample rate the app does not explicitly support. A rate the app supports is one it asks for or exposes in its own settings (a documented command-line switch/cvar/config); a capped ALSA device (s31route max_rate) or AUDIODEV steering is forcing and forbidden. Every fps taken through s31route_11k/22k (19.5-21.6 at 11 kHz, 17.7 at 22 kHz) is a forced-rate number; the honest baseline is 48 kHz through 'default'.

facts.claim: Why 48 kHz costs so much in 0.71: every cached sound is resampled to shm->speed at load (stepscale = info->rate/shm->speed, alloc_samples = samples/stepscale; snd_mem.c:455-470) and padded with the snd_filterquality window, so at 48 kHz the sound cache is ~48000/11025 = 4.35x the native 11 kHz data, and mixing does ~4.4x the work; the heap that fits at 22 kHz/-mem 10 (09-11) does not at 48 kHz, hence -mem 20 and 18.3 MB of swap. Estimated paging cost at 8.0 fps: 6,601 faults x ~3.3 ms (the review's per-fault cost) = 21.8 s of 120.9 s = 18% of the demo - a different regime from tiopex's ~900 faults/6.2 MB swap where paging was <1%.

facts.claim: C86 vs C87 rule boundary: C86 (replace libc.so's own soft-double math - floor/ceil/trunc/modf by integer bit tricks, float trig in single precision, s31fp's mul/add linked into libc.so ahead of libgcc) is platform and 'the legal part', priced at +1.2-3.5% of CPU0 on the tiopex profile (__adddf3 201 + __muldf3 94 + __subdf3 60 + __truncdfsf2 25 = 380/12,000 samples = 3.17%; s31fp does not improve add/sub, which are 67% of the block). C87 - rootfs/s31fp/libs31fp.so's LD_PRELOAD that finds libgcc's __muldf3/__adddf3/__subdf3/__floatsidf/__floatunsidf/__fixdfsi INSIDE the app's own text by byte signature and overwrites their entry with a jump - was rated 'the redline route' by the review's history lens, and the memory note records it 'Built, verified, NOT enabled'. facts.claim: The 48 kHz sound cache is why -mem 20 is needed: every sfx is resampled to shm->speed at load (alloc_samples = samples / (rate/speed), so 11,025 Hz sources grow 4.35x at 48 kHz) into Cache_Alloc inside the hunk, and shm->buffer is a hunk allocation sized by speed; the resampled cache is the ~8.5 MB allocation that fails at -mem 13/16 via Hunk_AllocName_Raw's 'Not enough RAM' path. -sndspeed N is the app's own documented switch (snd_sdl.c:79) and -mem N its own heap switch; the plan already recorded the 11 kHz vs 48 kHz swap footprint on the 0.62 engine as VmSwap 6.2 vs 8.3 MB at -mem 10.

facts.claim: CMA is 3 MiB reusable (reg 0x50800000 0x300000, PAGE_BLOCK_ORDER 8 makes 1 MiB granularity legal). It counts in MemTotal and holds movable pages (CmaFree 324 kB idle with the desktop), so shrinking it returns no MemTotal (4->0 MiB measured 15,456 kB both ways; 4->2 MiB gave +136 kB). Its free pages cannot satisfy GFP_KERNEL allocations, which is what produced the '6 MB free' OOM and why watermark_boost_factor=0 ships. What the pool must hold under a fullscreen game: the driver's scanout buffer 768,000 B (reserved at probe by espressif,scanout-size, permanent) plus the client's XRGB8888 plane for PPA scaling (320x240x4 = 307,200 B) and a small cursor ARGB buffer; the 2.25 MB ceiling (scanout + one 800x480x32 client) is why 3 MiB was chosen. lvdesk's own 770 kB render target is gone under direct scanout.
facts.evidence: esp32s31.dtsi:21-172 (comments carry the measurements); Makefile:638,732 (PAGE_BLOCK_ORDER); docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md dead-end #30; docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:346-348; memory note s31-watermark-boost-oom; linux-71-port/drivers/gpu/drm/espressif/esp32s31-lcd.c:1084-1099 (reserve at probe), 3443-3450 (XRGB8888 fullscreen plane), 3254 (cur_argb); docs/scanout-direct-plan.md:9-16; artifacts/gate/20260924-023423/contract.log:14

levers.why: Pure watermark: measured +744 kB of MemAvailable at idle with MemFree unchanged. It was raised from 256 to 1024 for streaming-read throughput (kswapd room: 5.11 -> 6.21 MB/s, CoreMark under load 313 -> 401), a workload the game does not run; under a swapping game the reserve is exactly the space kswapd needs to keep ahead of the allocator, so the sign is uncertain.
levers.expected_effect: +0.5-0.7 MB nominal headroom (measured idle +744 kB); fps effect priced by the review at +0.2 fps with unreliable sign; risk of synchronous reclaim in the fault path. Run D (09-19) combined it with swappiness 0 and is confounded; a clean fresh-boot pair on the -mem 12 configuration is the experiment.
levers.evidence: docs/current-state.md:6548-6552; overlay/etc/sysctl.d/99-s31-memory.conf:1-17; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:319 (C50); docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:283-286 (Run D)

levers.lever: C51: stop starting udevd (remove S10udevd, do not substitute mdev)
levers.why: Nothing consumes its rules: devtmpfs makes the nodes, lvdesk watches /dev/input itself, HID is hosted on hart0, CONFIG_UHID is off. Its 160 kB anon + 80 kB /run/udev tmpfs are true unreclaimable RAM (its 200 kB of SD text is clean cache and already evictable). Also removes ~1.8 s of rcS and the nice-19 coldplug.
levers.expected_effect: +~240 kB certain (up to ~440 kB counting the cache it stops competing for); ~0 fps on Quake per the review's physics lens, 18-34% more idle headroom. Risks recorded: USB/BT hotplug semantics and anything reading /run/udev; verify hotplug first. Not a lever for the 20 MB heap on its own (240 kB of an ~18 MB swap deficit).
levers.evidence: docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:178; docs/current-state.md:4915-4920 (udev not run: rcS 37.1 vs 43.0 s), 6554-6556, 3942 (UHID off); overlay/etc/init.d/S10udevd:31-63

levers.lever: Drop mlockall(MCL_CURRENT) in s31-bt, keep the per-buffer mlock of the audio path
levers.why: The daemon already pins its streaming buffers individually (s31-bt.c:1570-1591); MCL_CURRENT additionally pins every page resident at startup (dbus, libc data, its own heap), which can never swap even while no A2DP stream exists during a game. Bluetooth stays fully enabled.
levers.expected_effect: Makes an estimated 100-200 kB swappable rather than free (the 212 kB Mlocked audit figure is from before the MCL_FUTURE removal; the current locked size is not recorded). Worth ~0 fps; it only matters if a page-fault-free audio path is verified by ear afterwards.
levers.evidence: rootfs/s31-bt.c:1570-1591,2121-2139; docs/current-state.md:6541-6545 (audit: whole Mlocked figure is s31-bt)

levers.lever: Drop cold whole objects from S31_FAST_OBJS (X1-11a) now that C39 places hot functions by name
levers.why: .text..fast is still 235,520 B of PSRAM; before DCE 220,898 B of the region took zero samples in 12,000. DCE and the 24.3 kB agg-hot list changed the region, so the cold share must be re-resolved against the #363+ map before cutting - and the C23/C39 results show layout moves alone swing pingpong by +-15%, so the cut must be measured on pingpong, not assumed free.
levers.expected_effect: Up to ~150-200 kB of RAM (estimate; the pre-DCE figure was 180-220 kB), ~0 fps, real for desktop headroom. The review's other RAM item (shrinking .text..fast to 16 kB, X3-2) is rejected because it reverses four measured wins.

levers.lever: vm.page-cluster 2 -> 3 in physical-slot mode (vma_ra_enabled=0), judged on SDSTAT reads and majflt
levers.why: The -mem 20 run shows ~11.4 KiB average reads, i.e. page-cluster 2 is merging ~3 slots per request; 8 slots per request would cost 2.49 + 0.67 = 3.16 ms for 32 KiB instead of ~2.73 ms for 11 KiB. Physical-slot neighbours are what the game swapped out together, so hit rate is plausible, but at 436 kB MemAvailable every speculative page evicts a resident one - the review put a 30-40% regression chance on cluster 3, and the 4 KiB floor arithmetic needs ~75% hits to break even.
levers.expected_effect: If hits hold: ~-40% requests for the same pages, ~-8 s of the ~23 s paging tax on the -mem 20 run (estimate); if not, more evictions and a slower run. Only worth running on the -mem 12 configuration after it exists, fresh boot per arm, judged on fields 1 and 3 of /sys/block/mmcblk0/stat.
levers.evidence: artifacts/quake/td-tyr071-2-020026/run.log SDSTAT; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:157-159,245; overlay/etc/sysctl.d/99-s31-memory.conf:93-99

levers.lever: zram tier sizing (small pool with mem_limit, compression ratio measured first)
levers.why: Rejected four times: the pool is RAM taken from a machine at 436-800 kB free, so every MB of pool evicts a MB of the game and the kernel swaps more to fill it; the 512 kB cap made it inert in one run and a 2,984 kB-through-a-window thrash in another. Reads through zram avoid the 2.5 ms SD request, but decompression is PSRAM-bandwidth-bound (13.6 MB/s copy ceiling) - the scarcest resource. The unrecorded number is the compression ratio (mm_stat); if game heap compresses <2x it cannot pay at any size.
levers.expected_effect: Expected zero or negative per the record (review: +0.5-1.5%, not separable from zero; s31-swap.conf: MemAvailable 476 vs 2,932 kB with it on). Revisit only if MemAvailable under the game is a few MB, which the -mem 12 arm might produce; then an 8 MB disksize / 1 MB mem_limit arm with orig/compr from /sys/block/zram0/mm_stat recorded.
levers.evidence: overlay/etc/s31-swap.conf (whole file); docs/current-state.md:2046-2066; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:241,318, dead-end #2; kernel CONFIG_ZRAM=y (esp32s31_defconfig)

levers.lever: CMA 3 MiB -> 2 MiB (0x200000; PAGE_BLOCK_ORDER 8 already makes it legal)
levers.why: Reusable CMA is already counted in MemTotal and filled with movable pages, so the only gain is more memory usable by unmovable (GFP_KERNEL) allocations - measured +136 kB for 4->2. Under a 320x240 game the pool needs ~1.05 MB (768,000 scanout + 307,200 XRGB8888 client plane), so 2 MiB would fit this app, but the 800x480x32 client case (2.25 MB) the 3 MiB was chosen for would fail with 'scaling off' or a black panel.
levers.expected_effect: ~+0.1 MB (measured for a 2 MiB cut), 0 fps; breaks the fullscreen ceiling for larger clients. Not recommended.

levers.lever: Place the swap file on the fastest SD region
levers.why: No measurement of SD speed versus offset exists in the repo (not found). The measured cost model is per request, 2.49 ms + size/48 MB/s, taken at random offsets with a ~2.0 ms transaction floor, so region can only touch the size/48 MB/s term.
levers.expected_effect: Estimate: <= 0.08 ms of a ~2.6-2.7 ms page read (~3%), i.e. under 1 s of the ~28 s paging tax on the -mem 20 run; ~0 fps. Not worth an SD rewrite.
levers.evidence: docs/current-state.md:1745-1760,2036-2044,2072; memory note s31-read-is-memory-bound

levers.why: 0 OOM-kills Quake with the swap untouched (worklog 09-19, dead-end #20); higher values evict the game's anon heap sooner in favour of file pages that are already free to drop (XIP text) - the wrong direction for a heap-bound app; review C53/X1-28: -2% to +0.5%, more likely negative.
levers.expected_effect: Closed at 10.
levers.evidence: docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:287-293; overlay/etc/sysctl.d/99-s31-memory.conf:19-66; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:321

levers.lever: read_ahead_kb for pak reads (128 KB shipped; confirm the card's live value)
levers.why: Quake loads pak data with read() into the hunk, so each miss admits a read_ahead_kb window of page cache at ~436 kB free, evicting game pages; the demo's own stream is only ~780 kB at ~13 kB/s, and swap faults never touch read_ahead_kb. The 512 KB era read 98 MB per Doom demo; 16 vs 128 has been argued both ways and the card may hold either.
levers.expected_effect: ~0% on Quake (review X1-32); at most a few hundred kB of transient page cache. Read the live value in the next run's KNOBS line rather than tune it.

levers.lever: Evict or free desktop memory before launch (lvdesk MADV_PAGEOUT, pre-eviction, LV_MEM_SIZE)
levers.why: Rejected on mechanism: MADV_PAGEOUT skips folios mapped more than once (every xshim surface) and only queues SD writes; the reachable platform pool is ~450 kB gross (X1-29, 0 to +1%); LVGL's 400 KiB pool is a static array of which only touched pages (~25 kB) are resident; mlockall on lvdesk was measured 2x worse for input lag. facts.claim: C86 as built (rootfs/s31fp) is an LD_PRELOAD that patches, at load time and by libgcc byte signature, the soft-double helpers inside EVERY loaded executable segment including the main program: __muldf3 (asm, 738 -> 296 ns, 2.5x), __adddf3/__subdf3 (asm, add/sub mix 423 -> 308 ns, 1.4x), __floatsidf/__floatunsidf/__fixdfsi (conv.S). It does not touch __divdf3, __extendsfdf2, __truncdfsf2 or the compares. All 9 signatures in sigs.h match byte-for-byte the copies statically linked into rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg (checked today by reading the ELF at __muldf3 0x745c2, __adddf3 0x7359e, __subdf3 0x74b16, __divdf3 0x73da0, __extendsfdf2 0x772be, __truncdfsf2 0x7745c, __floatsidf 0x7546c, __fixdfsi 0x7532a, __floatunsidf 0x754bc). It is enabled nowhere: no LD_PRELOAD/s31fp in lvdesk/*.c, overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf or overlay/etc/profile.d.
facts.evidence: rootfs/s31fp/preload.c:1-30,47-54,100-143; rootfs/s31fp/build.sh:8; rootfs/s31fp/sigs.h; docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:525-541 ('Left built, verified, NOT enabled'); memory s31-soft-double-cost (dblbench: __muldf3 705-723 ns, __adddf3 420 ns, float mul 24 ns).

facts.claim: TyrQuake 0.71's double footprint is the same as 0.62's and is NOT in the pixel loops. Static call-site census of rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg (llvm-objdump): __extendsfdf2 199, __truncdfsf2 154, __muldf3 111, __adddf3 83, __subdf3 70, __ltdf2 41, __gtdf2 31, __floatsidf 19, __divdf3 16, __floatunsidf 10, __nedf2 5 (0.62: 182/144/107/70/70/35/27/15/11/4). Hot-by-site: SV_RunClients 35, V_AddIdle 34, SV_Physics 31, R_GenerateSpans 26 (R_LeadingEdge inlined; `double fu, newzi, testzi` at common/r_edge.c:421,680), SCR_UpdateScreen 25, CL_RelinkEntities 17, Q_atof 15 (parse time). Sources: explicit doubles host_frametime/host_time/realtime (NQ/host.c:64-66), cl.time/mtime (NQ/client.h:181-182), sv.time (NQ/server.h:37), FloorDivMod/Invert24To16 (common/mathlib.c:551-577,620-628), and double libm entry points imported from libc (atan atan2 atanf atof cosf exp floor ldexp logf pow sin sinf tan; AngleVectors uses double sin/cos at mathlib.c:317-324). D_DrawSpans8 (11.9% of CPU0 in the 0.62 profile) contains no soft-double call; only the *_Fence variants do (11 each). -fsingle-precision-constant (rootfs/build-tyrquake.sh:23) is what keeps float*literal on the FPU.

facts.claim: Measured ceiling for all libc math on this engine: in the only Quake PC profile (tiopex 0.62, SDL 1.2, 11 kHz, -mem 10, kernel #338, 17.1 fps, 12,000 samples) __adddf3 201 + __muldf3 94 + __subdf3 60 + __truncdfsf2 25 = 380 samples = 3.17% of CPU0, libm bodies 109 = 0.91%, absolute ceiling 4.17%. Review's honest range for the full C86 (floor family bit-exact + float trig in single precision + s31fp linked into libc.so): +1.2-3.5% of CPU0 -> +0.2-0.6 fps on a 16.6 fps boot, parts not additive. musl's float trig really is double inside: images/libc.nm has __sindf/__cosdf/__tandf/__rem_pio2f, and libc.so carries its own __adddf3/__muldf3/__divdf3 (libc.nm 0x674a0/0x6902c/0x68310). C87 (redirecting the app's statically linked copies) is what the review calls 'the redline route', worth ~0.2-0.3% of CPU0 more than C86 - and the app-side patching is exactly what preload.c does.

Non-idle kernel = 31.5% of CPU0, classified by symbol: irq entry/dispatch 6.0% (esp32s31_clic_handle_irq 93, handle_exception 50, handle_percpu_devid_irq 39, add_interrupt_randomness 30), scheduler/load-avg 5.5% (__schedule 78, __update_load_avg_se 59, update_curr_dl_se 43), timers/timekeeping 4.5% (__timekeeping_advance 56, ktime_get 47, tick_program_event 25), mm faults/page cache 2.4%, spinlocks 2.3%, syscall/poll 1.2% (do_sys_poll 34, do_trap_ecall_u 21), block/mmc 1.1%, memcpy/memset 0.8%, display 0.7% (esp32s31_lcd_copy_one 24), audio 0.4%, i2c/touch 0.3%, other 5.4%. facts.claim: Buildroot libraries already carry the S31 ISA except Zcb/Zcmp. Every userspace object (rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg, images/libSDL2-2.0.so.0.3200.10, libs31fp.so, libasound_module_pcm_s31route.so) has Tag_RISCV_arch rv32i2p1_m2p0_a2p1_f2p2_c2p0_b1p0_zicsr_zifencei_zmmul_zaamo_zalrsc_zca_zcf_zba_zbb_zbc_zbs_xespv2p2, and the app uses them (tyr-quake: 917 sh2add, 482 sh1add, 158 sh3add, 136 max, 121 min, 134 zext.h, 107 rev8, 101 bseti, 72 bexti, 48 ctz ... ~2,600 of 148,794 instructions; 0 cm.push / c.zext.b). Sources of the flags: BR2_RISCV_ISA_EXTRA=zaamo_zalrsc_zba_zbb_zbc_zbs_xespv2p2 and BR2_TARGET_OPTIMIZATION="-Os -march=rv32imafbc_zicsr_zifencei_zaamo_zalrsc_zba_zbb_zbc_zbs -mabi=ilp32 -mtune=esp-base" (buildroot-external/configs/esp32s31_rootfs_defconfig:11,24), S31_USER_ISA (Makefile:38, no zcb_zcmp; the kernel's S31_SAFE_ISA gets them under ZC=1 at Makefile:26-30), crosstool CT_ARCH_ARCH (configs/riscv32-esp-linux-musl.config:28, so musl and libgcc lack them too; CT_LIBC_MUSL_OPTIMIZE_SIZE=y :43). The Buildroot wrapper injects BR2_TARGET_OPTIMIZATION before the package's own flags (buildroot/toolchain/toolchain-wrapper.mk:19-22, toolchain-wrapper.c:390-401 adds -march only when the command line has none), so libSDL2 is -Os and tyr-quake's own -O2 (build-tyrquake.sh:23) wins for the app - and the app's -march comes from the wrapper, not from its build script.
facts.evidence: llvm-readelf --arch-specific on the four objects; llvm-objdump instruction census; the config lines cited; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:337 (musl 1.2.5 via crosstool-NG, not Buildroot's 1.2.6).

facts.claim: libSDL2 (and libc.so, libSDL2_mixer, libz, libpng) execute XIP from flash, the tier where the kernel work showed bytes-fetched-is-time (91% fetch-stalled on the kernel path), while the app itself runs from SD page cache in PSRAM. So code density of the libraries matters the way kernel density does, but their share of a Quake frame is small: 7.8% 'shared libraries' in the 0.62 profile, of which 4.2% is libc math (above); SDL2's own per-frame share in 0.71 is unmeasured. The 0.71 present path in library code per frame: the app expands 8-bit to 32-bit itself into an SDL_TEXTUREACCESS_STREAMING texture in the window's pixel format (vid_sdl.c:248-251, :441, :464-466 `dst32[i] = d_8to24table[src[i]]` - app code, untouchable), then SDL_RenderCopy + SDL_RenderPresent (vid_sdl.c:406-409) through SDL2's software renderer = at least one 307,200 B copy (320x240x4) plus the X11 put through xlite.
facts.evidence: Makefile:919-926 (XIP_ROOTS lists usr/lib/libSDL2-2.0.so.0.3200.10, libSDL2_mixer, libpng16, libz), Makefile:1106 (libc.so in the second image); memory s31-cache-counters; tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/vid_sdl.c lines cited; artifacts/quake/h1s-062518 split (libs 934/12,000).

facts.claim: TyrQuake 0.71 presents through an SDL2 STREAMING texture + SDL_RenderCopy + SDL_RenderPresent, never SDL_UpdateWindowSurface directly. VID_SetMode creates the window (vid_sdl.c:227-230), a renderer with SDL_RENDERER_PRESENTVSYNC because vid_vsync defaults to "1" (vid_sdl.c:234-239, vid_mode.c:116), and a streaming texture in the desktop's pixel format at mode size (vid_sdl.c:248-252). VID_Update locks the WHOLE texture (vid_sdl.c:440-441), expands 8-bit vid.buffer through d_8to16table/d_8to24table per damage rect (vid_sdl.c:456-481), unlocks, then VID_SDL_BlitRect does SDL_RenderCopy of the full 320x240 + SDL_RenderPresent (vid_sdl.c:399-410, 483). The copy is 1:1 because vid.output = mode size (vid_mode.c:145-146).
facts.evidence: tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/vid_sdl.c:225-252, 399-410, 413-484; common/vid_mode.c:116, 145-146

facts.claim: The SDL2 client runs at 16 bpp RGB565 (153,600 B/frame), NOT 32 bpp/300 kB as the brief assumed. SDL2 derives the desktop mode format from the X default visual: get_visualinfo uses DefaultDepth + XMatchVisualInfo(TrueColor) (SDL_x11modes.c:64-68), X11_GetPixelFormatFromVisualInfo takes bpp = vinfo->depth and the visual's masks (SDL_x11modes.c:90-120), and that becomes mode.format (SDL_x11modes.c:308, 345). xlite advertises root depth 16 with masks F800/07E0/001F (xlite/xlite.c:849, 886-891; xlite_req.c:3300-3308). The window and its framebuffer use displaydata->visual/depth (SDL_x11window.c:476-477; SDL_x11framebuffer.c:73-83, pitch = 320*2 = 640). TyrQuake then takes the PACKED16 branch (vid_sdl.c:469-476). The 32-bit path exists only if SDL_VIDEO_X11_WINDOW_VISUALID names xlite's depth-32 visual (SDL_x11window.c:431-442) and it measured worse: chocolate-doom 10.7 -> 5.5 fps (perf-review dead-end #81; xshim.c:8618-8620).
facts.evidence: artifacts/perf-plan/sdl2-src-ro/x11/SDL_x11modes.c:64-68, 90-120, 286-308, 345; x11/SDL_x11window.c:431-442, 476-477; x11/SDL_x11framebuffer.c:73-83; xlite/xlite.c:849, 886-891; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:470

facts.claim: The software renderer is the ONLY render driver compiled: SDL_config.h in the Buildroot tree defines no SDL_VIDEO_RENDER_OGL*/OPENGL symbols (grep returned nothing), so SDL_CreateRenderer(-1, PRESENTVSYNC) takes the driver loop at SDL_render.c:1020-1035 and lands on SW_CreateRenderer (SDL_render_sw.c:1035-1063), which calls SDL_GetWindowSurface. There is no GL probe cost and no way to select anything else.
facts.evidence: docker: /src/build/buildroot/build/sdl2-2.32.10/include/SDL_config.h (no SDL_VIDEO_RENDER_ defines; SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_X11 1, X11_XRANDR 1, X11_XINPUT2 1); sdl2-src-ro/render/SDL_render.c:1020-1035; sw/SDL_render_sw.c:1035-1063

facts.claim: Simulated vsync does NOT engage despite vid_vsync=1: the SW driver claims SDL_RENDERER_PRESENTVSYNC in its info.flags (SDL_render_sw.c:1070), so SDL_CreateRenderer leaves simulate_vsync false (SDL_render.c:1057-1063), and SDL_RenderPresent only calls SDL_RenderSimulateVSync/SDL_Delay when simulate_vsync or !presented (SDL_render.c:4307-4310). X11_UpdateWindowFramebuffer has no vsync wait. So the app believes vsync is on (vsync_available = true, vid_sdl.c:245) but pays nothing; SDL_RENDER_VSYNC=0 in the environment would change nothing.
facts.evidence: sdl2-src-ro/sw/SDL_render_sw.c:1066-1080; render/SDL_render.c:1057-1063, 4262-4310; x11/SDL_x11framebuffer.c:151-201

facts.claim: The texture is native RGB565 (in SW's texture_formats, SDL_render_sw.c:1073-1080), so SDL_LockTexture is a direct pointer into the texture's SDL_Surface with no staging copy (SW_LockTexture SDL_render_sw.c:157-167, SW_UnlockTexture is empty 169-171). No RLE encode/decode per frame: SW_CreateTexture only requests RLE for SDL_TEXTUREACCESS_STATIC (117-121) and SDL_RLESurface refuses surfaces without colorkey/alpha blend anyway (SDL_RLEaccel.c:1426-1434).
facts.evidence: sdl2-src-ro/sw/SDL_render_sw.c:101-127, 157-171, 1073-1080; video/SDL_RLEaccel.c:1407-1434

facts.claim: Per-frame client byte path (SDL2, 320x240 fullscreen): (1) VID_Update: 76,800 one-byte reads + 76,800 halfword table lookups + 153,600 B written into the texture surface (vid_sdl.c:469-476); (2) SDL_RenderCopy -> SW_RunCommandQueue COPY, same-size so SDL_BlitSurface (SDL_render_sw.c:802-803) -> SDL_BlitCopy row memcpy 153,600 B from the texture into the MIT-SHM window surface (SDL_blit_copy.c:91-130); (3) SW_RenderPresent -> SDL_UpdateWindowSurface (SDL_render_sw.c:964-971) -> X11_UpdateWindowFramebuffer: ONE XShmPutImage of the whole window with send_event False + XSync (SDL_x11framebuffer.c:151-171, 199); (4) xlite XShmPutImage is a 40-byte request, no flush (xlite_req.c:2824-2887), XSync = GetInputFocus round trip that blocks until the server replies (xlite.c:1018-1046). MIT-SHM is live for SDL2 because xstubs' libXext.so.6 forwards XShm* to xlite (xstubs/xstubs.c:163-202) and the segment is SysV shmget/shmat (SDL_x11framebuffer.c:86-125; xlite XShmAttach + XSync xlite_req.c:2737-2763).
facts.evidence: vid_sdl.c:469-476; sdl2-src-ro/sw/SDL_render_sw.c:785-803, 964-971; video/SDL_blit_copy.c:91-130; x11/SDL_x11framebuffer.c:86-125, 151-201; xlite/xlite_req.c:2737-2763, 2824-2887; xlite/xlite.c:1018-1046; xstubs/xstubs.c:163-202

facts.claim: Server side, the 153,600 B ShmPutImage copy is on the client's critical path. xshim's ShmPutImage handler copies from the SysV segment into the window buffer with a per-row FNV-1a hash (xshim.c:5377-5560; bpp = window bpp = 2, 5410-5417), damages only changed rows, then late_present_queue (5594-5595). Replies leave at the end of client_data() and only THEN late_present_drain runs (xshim.c:9633-9638), so the client's XSync returns after the copy but before lvdesk's present. The copy is deliberately never replaced by adopting the segment ("COPY. Always." xshim.c:5422-5450: adopting gave +11% but flickered and is not a legal implementation). Late present is on by default (xshim.c:520-570, +13% Doom).

Fullscreen path: SDL_WINDOW_FULLSCREEN -> SDL_SetDisplayModeForDisplay -> X11_SetDisplayMode -> XRRSetCrtcConfig (SDL_x11modes.c:743-804) -> xlite's libXrandr shim (xlite/randr/xrandr.c:386) -> xshim RANDR SetCrtcConfig (xshim.c:8244-8270) -> vm_switch -> mode_cb -> lvdesk xwin_on_mode (lvdesk.c:4245-4276) -> kms_fs_enter(320,240,16) (kms.c:662-745) -> DRM mode 320x240 -> esp32s31_lcd_place_mode: k = min(800*16/320, 480*16/240) = 32 -> 640x480 at +80+0, PPA-scaled (esp32s31-lcd.c:1476-1543). The EWMH _NET_WM_STATE request SDL2 also sends (SDL_x11window.c:1363-1420, 1526-1528) hits xshim's SendEvent handler (xshim.c:7647-7690) -> ewmh_fullscreen, which picks the same 320x240 from vm_modes (xshim.c:403-405, 418-432). 320x240 is in the RandR mode list SDL2 enumerates (xshim.c:8098-8125), so TyrQuake's -width 320 -height 240 -fullscreen resolves to a real mode and the window stays 320x240 (no CPU upscale in SDL).
facts.evidence: sdl2-src-ro/x11/SDL_x11modes.c:743-804; x11/SDL_x11window.c:1363-1420, 1526-1528; xlite/randr/xrandr.c:386; lvdesk/xshim.c:403-405, 418-432, 7647-7690, 8244-8270; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:4245-4276; lvdesk/kms.c:662-776; linux-71-port/drivers/gpu/drm/espressif/esp32s31-lcd.c:1476-1543

facts.claim: lvdesk's fullscreen present of a 16-bit window is a plain memcpy, after the reply, on lvdesk's hart: fs_present (lvdesk.c:4720-4880) gets NULL from xshim_window_indices (bpp != 1, xshim.c:8552-8555), xshim_window_raw reports bpp 2 so the 32-bit branch is skipped, xshim_window_pixels returns r->px for bpp 2 (xshim.c:8783), and the damaged rows are memcpy'd into kms_fs_map (lvdesk.c:4862-4865) followed by kms_fs_dirty -> DRM_IOCTL_MODE_DIRTYFB (kms.c:757-776) -> esp32s31_lcd_copy_one per lattice-snapped rect, PPA SRM 2x upscale with ppa_async (esp32s31-lcd.c:2049-2185, 1238-1240). Row-skip hashing is off by default (LVDESK_ROWSKIP, lvdesk.c:4690-4705). None of this is on the client's critical path (late present) and lvdesk lives on CPU1 which is 63.7% idle during a timedemo (perf-plan.md:209-211), so lvdesk/driver savings are 0% on client fps by construction (perf-review T2.7 argument, lines 219-221).

SDL 1.2 8bpp (tiopex) comparison path: SDL_UpdateRects -> XPutImage -> xlite XliteShmMap cache hit -> per-row memcpy of 76,800 B straight into the shared window pages + XliteShmDamaged (no reply; xlite_req.c:3524-3548, 3065-3110), then SDL 1.2's own XSync round trip; server pre-reply work is two tiny requests; lvdesk expands 8->RGB565 into kms_fs_map on CPU1 at a MEASURED 3.06 ms per 320x240 frame (lvdesk.c comment "scalar, paired 32-bit stores 3062 us", ~4885-4900). Client critical-path bytes: 76.8 kB written. SDL2 client critical-path bytes: 76.8 kB read + 153.6 kB written (expand) + 153.6 kB read + 153.6 kB written (blit) + 153.6 kB read + 153.6 kB written in xshim before the reply = ~845 kB, i.e. ~5.5x, plus the 8->16 palette expansion moved from the idle hart onto the client's hart.
facts.evidence: xlite/xlite_req.c:3065-3110, 3524-3548; lvdesk/lvdesk.c ~4885-4900 (measured 3062 us)

facts.claim: ESTIMATE of the SDL2 client's per-frame present cost at 320x240 (quiet board), from measured anchors: expand loop 76,800 px x 49-66 ns/px (dead-end #9 expander numbers) = 3.8-5.1 ms; SDL_BlitCopy of 153,600 B = 3.09 ms quiet / 11.98 ms loaded (accel-plan.md table row "320x240 153600 3.09 / 2.99 ms 11.98 / 6.96 ms", CPU column, a row-by-row memcpy of exactly this size); xshim copy+hash of 153,600 B >= 3.09 ms (same copy plus 38,400 xor+mul) blocking the client; cross-hart wake round trip ~1.0 ms (pingpong cross-hart 1,035-1,044 us, plan Phase 3). Sum ~11-12.3 ms quiet, more when loaded. SDL 1.2 8bpp equivalent: 76.8 kB memcpy ~1.5 ms + round trip ~1 ms = ~2.5 ms. Delta ~8.5-10 ms per frame = 15-18% of a 55.6 ms frame (tiopex's 17.5-18.2 fps with sound). So the same engine on the SDL2 path would land near 15-16 fps even with the swap term removed, before any engine-version difference. The only SDL2 vs SDL1 measurement that exists is the canary: sdl2-indexed-timers 24.2-27.5 ms vs sdl1-indexed 12.3-14.7 ms per 320x200 frame (perf-plan.md:331, 437, 697, 714; rootfs/sdlbench2.c:10), but that canary uses an ARGB8888 texture with an 8->32 convert and a 32->16 blit, so it is heavier than tyr-quake's 16-bit path and only bounds it.

facts.claim: Memory footprint of the SDL2 pipeline is larger than SDL1's by ~460 kB of resident buffers: texture surface 153.6 kB + SysV SHM segment 153.6 kB (client side, both touched every frame) + xshim window px 153.6 kB + a 153.6 kB CMA dumb buffer for the 320x240 mode (kms_fs_enter), versus SDL1's 76.8 kB shared pixmap (+ SDL1's own 76.8 kB XImage). At 436 kB MemAvailable during the demo this is not free. libSDL2-2.0.so.0.3200.10 (1,166,260 B on target) IS in the XIP image list (Makefile:922), so its text costs no RSS.
facts.evidence: Makefile:920-925; sdl2-src-ro/x11/SDL_x11framebuffer.c:86-100; lvdesk/kms.c:662-745; artifacts/quake/td-tyr071-2-020026/run.log

facts.claim: Prior verdicts that this subsystem must not re-litigate: MIT-SHM segment adoption (31.7 fps but flickers, illegal - dead-end #15, xshim.c:5422-5450); XLITE-SHM answer cache measured nothing; PPA CLUT expansion -7.5% windowed (dead-end #11); windowed 32-bit SDL2 visual lost three times (#81); XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT bounded the SDL1 'last round trip' family at <=2.5% Quake and was CLOSED (perf-plan.md:98-101), knob kept in xlite.c:1002-1046; C89 'SDL2 software-renderer fast paths' was rated violates-rules/refuted on the ground that no goal app linked libSDL2 (perf-review.md:369) - that ground is now stale because rootfs/tyr-quake does, but the violates-rules lens stands; C94/X3-11 route (a) with ShmCompletion needs SDL-side consumption that stock SDL2 lacks (SDL_x11framebuffer.c:170 passes False and nothing reads the event).

SDL2's event pump per frame is cheap under XLITE-RING: X11_PumpEvents -> X11_PollEvent -> X11_XPending -> xlite XEventsQueued does a non-blocking ring read (xlite.c:1050-1078 -> xlite_ring_read_more with block=0, 412-448), which costs one eventfd read only when the doorbell is set and no poll() otherwise. The XSync reply wait is where the client sleeps (poll on efd_in, xlite.c:437-449 / xlite_reply at xlite.c:644).

SDL2 sources read for this analysis were copied out of the Docker build volume to /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/artifacts/perf-plan/sdl2-src-ro/ (untracked; x11/, render/, sw/, video/ subsets of sdl2-2.32.10). Line numbers cited as sdl2-src-ro/... refer to those copies, which are byte-identical to /src/build/buildroot/build/sdl2-2.32.10/src/...
facts.evidence: artifacts/perf-plan/sdl2-src-ro/

levers.lever: xshim: stop hashing rows for a fullscreen 16-bit ShmPutImage target (or stand the hash down adaptively when a scan keeps <1/8 of rows, like lvdesk's fsrh_probe in lvdesk.c:4700-4730), so the pre-reply copy is a plain memcpy. Measure first with the existing XSHIM_NOROWDMG=1 knob (xshim.c:614-624), no build.
levers.why: The 38,400 xor+mul+store per frame in xshim.c:5500-5545 sit on the client's critical path (the XSync reply follows the copy, xshim.c:9633-9638). For an action game every row changes every frame (prboom kept 59 rows of 2,031,184, lvdesk.c:4690-4700), so the hash buys nothing and lvdesk presents all rows anyway.
levers.expected_effect: Estimate 0.3-0.6 ms per frame off the client's blocking window (38,400 iterations x ~3-5 cycles at 320 MHz), i.e. <=1% at 55 ms frames. Only resolvable bundled or on the xsp per-op timer (XSHIM_PROF ShmPutImage ns), never on fps alone.

levers.lever: xlite: XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT=1 on tyr-quake as a BOUND on the whole pre-reply-copy + round-trip family (same-boot A/B/A, A-to-A gap as the error bar). Not a shippable default: the client has no completion guarantee, so an lvdesk stall longer than one game frame tears one frame.
levers.why: The plan closed this family at <=2.5% on the SDL1 canary (perf-plan.md:98-101), where the server's pre-reply work was two tiny requests. For SDL2 the pre-reply work is a 153,600 B copy+hash (>=3.09 ms measured for that size, accel-plan.md:35) plus the ~1 ms cross-hart wake, so the family's ceiling must be re-measured on this client. The SDL2 client writes the SHM segment only in the RenderCopy blit immediately before the next XShmPutImage (SDL_render_sw.c:802-803 -> 964-971), so in practice the race window is xshim's ~3 ms copy against the client's ~50 ms frame; it is still a race by construction, and no legal xlite-only ordering exists because the client's next segment write precedes its next XShmPutImage (the T2.4 'defer the wait to the next put' variant is unsafe for SDL2).
levers.expected_effect: Estimate 4-5 ms per frame removed from the client's critical path = 7-9% at 55 ms frames IF the bound holds; the measured number is the ceiling for any legal lever in this family, which is why it is worth one boot before anything is built.
levers.evidence: xlite/xlite.c:1002-1046; docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:98-101; docs/accel-plan.md:35; sdl2-src-ro/sw/SDL_render_sw.c:785-803, 964-971

levers.lever: SDL2 (Buildroot shared library): make SW_LockTexture hand out the window surface's pixels when a STREAMING texture has the window surface's size and format and the renderer target is the window, so SDL_RenderCopy's same-size SDL_BlitSurface becomes a no-op and the 153,600 B texture->segment blit disappears.
levers.why: The task lists Buildroot-built libSDL2 as platform, but the memory redline (s31-never-rebuild-client-apps: 'no custom library') and C89's recorded violates-rules lens (perf-review.md:369) say a patched stock library is the thing the user forbade; C89's other ground ('no goal app links libSDL2') is stale now that rootfs/tyr-quake does. Flagged for the orchestrator to rule on, not recommended. Technically it is also fragile: the texture would alias the segment xshim reads, reintroducing exactly the read-while-drawing race adoption had (xshim.c:5422-5450), so it would only be safe with the XSync wait kept.
levers.expected_effect: Removes one 153,600 B copy from the client's critical path: 3.09 ms quiet / up to 11.98 ms loaded (accel-plan.md:35-36) = 5.5% of a 55 ms frame quiet.
levers.evidence: sdl2-src-ro/sw/SDL_render_sw.c:157-167, 785-803; docs/accel-plan.md:20-50; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:369; lvdesk/xshim.c:5422-5450

levers.lever: Keep the SDL2 client on the 16-bit default visual; do NOT set SDL_VIDEO_X11_WINDOW_VISUALID (32-bit) or any SDL render hint from menu.conf or /etc/lvdesk.env.
levers.why: Every hint-level knob is either inert or negative here: the software renderer is the only driver (no SDL_VIDEO_RENDER_* in SDL_config.h), SDL_RENDER_VSYNC changes nothing because the SW driver claims PRESENTVSYNC and X11_UpdateWindowFramebuffer never waits (SDL_render.c:1057-1063, 4307-4310), and the 32-bit visual doubles every copy and adds a 32->16 conversion (measured 10.7 -> 5.5 fps on chocolate-doom, #81). The correction that matters is to the record: the brief's '32 bpp, 300 kB/frame' premise is false for tyr-quake; it is 16 bpp, 153,600 B.
levers.expected_effect: 0% (a guard against a regression, and a correction of the brief), no measurement needed.
levers.evidence: sdl2-src-ro/x11/SDL_x11window.c:431-442; render/SDL_render.c:1057-1063, 4307-4310; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:470

levers.lever: xshim/lvdesk: in fullscreen at 16 bpp, let xshim's ShmPutImage copy land directly in kms_fs_map (the mode's framebuffer) instead of d->buf->px, deleting lvdesk's second 153,600 B memcpy in fs_present.
levers.why: Both copies exist today (xshim.c:5480-5560 then lvdesk.c:4862-4865). But the second one runs after the reply on lvdesk's hart, which is 63.7% idle during a timedemo, so removing it is 0% on client fps by construction (perf-review.md:219-221). The only client-visible effect is fewer collisions where the client's next ShmPutImage waits behind lvdesk's synchronous DIRTYFB; with a ~5-8 ms present per ~55 ms frame that is ~10-15% of frames x a few ms = ~0.5 ms/frame mean, an estimate. Also risks making the pre-reply copy slower if the dumb buffer's mapping is not cached (dead-end #10 says it is, at 7.6 MB/s if aliased uncached).
levers.expected_effect: ~0-1% on client fps (estimate); real only as CPU1 headroom. Not worth building before the XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT bound says the family is worth anything.
levers.evidence: lvdesk/xshim.c:5480-5560; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:4862-4865; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:219-221, 399

levers.lever: Launcher: keep the menu's Timedemo entry consistent with the harness (-fullscreen, quake-timedemo.sh:44) rather than -window (menu.conf), so measured and played paths are the same present path.
levers.why: Windowed presents go through LVGL compositing on lvdesk's hart (the 16-bit window is not eligible for xwin_blit_direct, which only handles indexed windows, lvdesk.c:5645-5662); fullscreen goes through fs_present + PPA 2x scale. Both are post-reply, so the client-side difference is the same ~0-1% collision term, but numbers taken on one path should not be quoted for the other.
levers.expected_effect: 0% on the client's critical path; removes a measurement inconsistency.
levers.evidence: buildroot-external/board/esp32-s31/overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf (Timedemo line); scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh:44; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:5645-5662

levers.lever: REJECTED: DMA (PPA/GDMA) for xshim's ShmPutImage copy.
levers.why: The SysV segment SDL2 creates with shmget (SDL_x11framebuffer.c:89) is ordinary memory; the PPA can only address lcd_reserved and esp32s31_ppa_in_range() refuses anything else (xshim.c:194-197). MIT-SHM 1.2 ShmCreateSegment (server-supplied fd) would fix that but stock SDL2 never uses it. The engine's completion wait is also 0.7-1.1 ms below ~128 kB (dead-end #7), the same order as the copy.
levers.expected_effect: 0 (not implementable for this client).
levers.evidence: sdl2-src-ro/x11/SDL_x11framebuffer.c:86-125; lvdesk/xshim.c:194-197; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:396-397

facts.claim: TyrQuake 0.71 asks SDL for 48000 Hz, 16-bit, stereo by default and takes WHATEVER rate the device grants: snd_sdl.c:35 SND_DEFAULT_RATE 48000; :79-81 honours -sndspeed N; :130 SDL_OpenAudio(&desired,&obtained) which in SDL 2.32.10 is SDL_AUDIO_ALLOW_ANY_CHANGE (SDL_audio.c:1589, obtained->freq = device freq at :1445-1450); :165 shm->speed = obtained.freq. The ALSA backend negotiates with snd_pcm_hw_params_set_rate_near (SDL_alsa_audio.c:714-719). So a rate-capped device silently changes the app's mixing rate (why the s31route_11k arm was a rule violation), and the only app-explicit rate control is -sndspeed (documented in man/tyrquake.6 'Specify sample speed for sound output').
facts.evidence: tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/snd_sdl.c:35,79-81,130,164-166; Buildroot sdl2-2.32.10 src/audio/SDL_audio.c:1445-1450,1589; src/audio/alsa/SDL_alsa_audio.c:714-719; man/tyrquake.6 '-sndspeed n'

facts.claim: Per-sound cache allocation is sizeof(sfxcache_t)+(samples*shm->speed/info->rate + pad)*info->width, plus a 56-byte cache_system_t header, rounded to 16 (snd_mem.c:455-470, zone.c Cache_AllocPadded). pad = filter window (16/32/64/128/256 for snd_filterquality 1..5, default 3 => 64 samples; halved for looped sounds) only when info->rate < shm->speed (snd_mem.c:464-468, :192, :178). Note loadas8bit does NOT shrink the allocation (Cache_Alloc uses info->width at :470; only ResampleSfx :71 honours it) and is auto-set only below an 8 MB heap (snd_dma.c:252-255); all but one of the 121 shareware sounds in demo1's precache are already 8-bit 11025 Hz mono, so it is inert here.
facts.evidence: tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/snd_mem.c:455-490,192,178,71; common/zone.c:1215-1224 (size = size+pad+sizeof(cache_system_t)+15 &~15); pak0.pak WAV headers parsed on the host (scratchpad q/pak.py): rate/width histogram {(11025,1ch,8-bit):120, (22050,16-bit):1}

facts.claim: The doc's mechanism for '-mem 20 is needed at 48 kHz because the ~8.5 MB resampled sound cache is the Hunk allocation that fails at -mem 13/16' is WRONG. Sounds are Cache allocations, and the cache can never make Hunk_AllocName fail: Hunk growth evicts/moves cache blocks (zone.c:920-960 Cache_FreeLow/High), and Cache_Alloc frees LRU entries until it fits (zone.c:1231-1245). The ~8.5 MB Hunk block is the SERVER EDICT TABLE: sv.edicts = MAX_EDICTS(8192) * pr_edict_size (sv_main.c:1355-1356, quakedef.h:74), pr_edict_size = entityfields*4 + edict header (pr_edict.c:1139); shareware progs.dat has entityfields=195 (780 B) and the header is 264 B on rv32 (free 4 + link_t 8 + num_leafs 4 + leafnums[48] 192 + entity_state_t 48 + alpha 1+3 + freetime 4) -> 1,044 B x 8192 = 8,552,448 B (8.16 MiB) on the board; measured 8,650,768 on the 64-bit host (1,056 B/edict, link_t 16). It exists only when a server runs (map/new game), not during a demo playback.

facts.claim: -mem needed (arithmetic, rv32 estimates): TIMEDEMO (no server): hunk current ~8.2 MB (+1.3 MB transient peak while the 1.25 MB bsp sits in the temp high hunk) + cache set -> 48 kHz: 8.2+8.9 = 17.1 -> -mem 18; 22050: 8.2+5.1 = 13.3 -> -mem 14; 11025: 8.2+3.5 = 11.7 -> -mem 12 (the in-flight arms sit exactly at the edge). REAL PLAY on e1m1 (server): current ~16.9 MB + cache -> 48 kHz: 25.8 -> -mem 26; 22050: 22.0 -> -mem 23; 11025: 20.4 -> -mem 21; below ~17.8 MB (peak) the map does not load at any rate, which is what '-mem 13 and 16 fail' actually measured. Since the heap is one malloc (sys_unix.c:371-372) and Hunk_AllocName memsets only what it hands out (zone.c:618-624) while the cache is written only as sounds/models land, a larger -mem costs nothing until used - but every byte that IS used is touched: the board runs show VmRSS+VmSwap = 22.9 MB at -mem 20/48k (4,592+18,340 kB), 16.9 MB at -mem 12/11k (4,748+12,172), 19.1 MB at -mem 14/22k (4,552+14,504), i.e. the whole heap plus ~4-5 MB of binary/libs/BSS.

facts.claim: Outside the heap, the board binary has a 6,243,216-byte .bss (rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg ELF): cl_static_entities 2,359,296 and cl_entities 2,359,296 (entity_t[8192], client.h:260,266-267), sv 807,424 (three 256 kB message buffers, server.h:59-65), packetBuffer 262,152, cl_efrags 131,072, snd_scaletable 32,768, channels 28,672, paintbuffer 16,384. CL_ClearState memsets cl_entities and cl_efrags (cl_main.c:125-126) and Host_ClearMemory memsets sv (host.c:480) on every connect/map, so ~3.3 MB of zero pages are touched per level in addition to the hunk memsets. The 7.1 kernel's swap zeromap never writes zero folios (docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:430, item 41), so once reclaimed these cost no SD traffic, but they are why VmSwap exceeds -mem.

facts.claim: Mixer cost per second (ESTIMATE, arithmetic shown; no board profile of the mixer exists - perf-plan:498 measured the whole main thread at 86% and the SDL audio thread at 5% at 48 kHz, perf-review:482 snd_* kernel side 0.46% at 11 kHz). S_PaintChannels (snd_mix.c:183-245) per output frame: memset 8 B, per active channel SND_PaintChannelFrom8_Generic (:291-295) = 1 byte load + 2 table loads + 2 paintbuffer RMW = ~10 instructions, then halve+clamp (:234-237, ~10 instr) and Snd_WriteLinearBlastStereo16 (:37-59, ~12 instr) -> ~22 + 10*N instr per frame. With N=4 active channels: 48,000*62 = 3.0 M instr/s; N=8: 4.9 M/s -> ~1-3% of the 320 MHz core at 0.5-1 IPC; at 22050: 0.5-1.4%; at 11025: 0.2-0.7%. Total mixed samples per second is fixed at the rate regardless of mixahead or how many S_Update/S_ExtraUpdate calls happen (S_Update_ paints from paintedtime up to soundtime + 0.1 s, snd_dma.c:879-884; S_ExtraUpdate is called ~4-5 times per frame from r_main.c:1104,1143,1230, r_edge.c:879, draw.c:1099,1115). The mixer arithmetic therefore cannot explain the 48k-vs-11k fps gap; the memory (cache 4.34x, swap, cache thrash + reload) does.
facts.evidence: common/snd_mix.c:183-245,262-299,37-59; common/snd_dma.c:853-888; docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:498-500; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:482; rootfs/s31route.c:541-543 (14.0 fps no sound vs 10.7 at 48 kHz with 868 vs 3,674 majflt)

facts.claim: Load-time (and every cache-miss reload) cost that DOES scale with rate: the windowed-sinc low-pass S_FilterSfx runs over every output sample whenever info->rate < shm->speed (snd_mem.c:486-487, :344-389): kernel_size = window-2 = 62 taps, unrolled x4 in float (:295-302, real FPU, single precision). ESTIMATE: 48 kHz: 7.09 M output samples x 64 MAC = 454 M MAC; 22050: 3.27 M x 64 = 209 M; 11025: 0 (cutoff_ratio 0.5 -> early return at :351, and no pad). At ~3-4 cycles per MAC (2 loads + fmadd.s per tap) that is ~5 s (48k) / ~2.3 s (22k) / 0 of CPU at map load, and per reload of a thrashed sound e.g. weapons/sgun1.wav 99,632 samples x 64 x 3.5 / 320 MHz = ~70 ms plus the SD read (2.49 ms + size/48 MB/s).
facts.evidence: common/snd_mem.c:295-302,344-389,464-468,486-487; scratchpad/q/pak.py per-sound table; CLAUDE.md SD request cost

facts.claim: SDL/ALSA buffering by rate: desired.samples = 1 << Q_log2(freq * _snd_mixahead(0.1) * 0.5) (snd_sdl.c:119, Q_log2 is floor) = 2048 frames at 48000, 1024 at 22050, 512 at 11025; SDL ALSA sets period = that and periods >= 2 (SDL_alsa_audio.c:544-561); the app ring shm->samples = 1 << Q_log2(speed*channels/2) = 32768/16384/8192 mono samples = 64/32/16 kB of hunk (snd_sdl.c:171-174; matches 'soundinfo' 32768/16384/8192 samples). The route plugin offers 8000..max_rate (default 48000) S16_LE only, 1-2 channels (rootfs/s31route.c:508-546), and the I2S sink mask is 8000/11025/16000/44100/48000/96000 - no 22050 (linux-71-port/sound/soc/espressif/esp32s31-i2s.c:520-523) - so a 22050 request is resampled by the 'plug' slave on the platform side (s31route.c:112-115). -sndbits 8 is inert here (plugin offers only S16, and the app accepts a granted S16, snd_sdl.c:140-148).
facts.evidence: common/snd_sdl.c:119,171-174,136-160; Buildroot sdl2-2.32.10 src/audio/alsa/SDL_alsa_audio.c:533-590; rootfs/s31route.c:508-546,112-115; linux-71-port/sound/soc/espressif/esp32s31-i2s.c:520-523

facts.claim: App-documented switches and cvars that change memory or CPU (man/tyrquake.6 unless noted): -mem N (MB) / -heapsize N (kB), default 256 MB (zone.c:1263-1277); -zone N kB (default 256 kB; the host run used 10,640 B in 231 blocks, 'zone print'); -minmemory (5.5 MB, fatal below MINIMUM_MEMORY 0x550000 quakedef.h:48); -sndspeed N; -sndbits 8|16 (code default 16, snd_sdl.c:34; the man page's 'Default 8/11025' is stale); -sndmono; -nosound (crashes upstream per docs/current-state.md:8488); -simsound; -noextmusic; -surfcachesize kB (d_surf.c:49-52); -particles N (default 2048 x 48 B = 98 kB, r_part.c:60-72); -window/-w, -width/-height, -fullscreen, -bpp (parsed for all targets at vid_mode.c:1218 despite the man page saying GL/Windows), -listen n (floored to 4 for memory purposes). Cvars (config.cfg / +cvar on the command line, but the user's rule forbids config steering for performance): snd_filterquality 0-5 (snd_mem.c:178; 0 disables the FIR and its pad), loadas8bit (inert here), _snd_mixahead 0.1 (CVAR_CONFIG, snd_dma.c:105), precache (snd_dma.c:97), ambient_level, r_maxsurfs/r_maxedges (r_main.c:132-133; MINSURFACES 768/MINEDGES 2304 live on the stack up to 6400/15360, r_shared.h:85-105), vid_vsync 1 (vid_mode.c:116 -> SDL_RENDERER_PRESENTVSYNC vid_sdl.c:234), vid_width/height/bpp defaults 800/600/32 (vid_mode.c:59-61), host_framerate, r_lerpmodels/r_lerpmove (r_alias.c:65-66).
facts.evidence: tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/man/tyrquake.6; grep of COM_CheckParm over NQ/common; the file:line references given inline

facts.claim: Board results now on record for stock 0.71 (fresh boot, demo1, 320x240 fullscreen, AUDIO=default): -mem 20 -sndspeed default 48000: 8.0 fps, majflt 6,601, VmRSS 4,592 kB, VmSwap 18,340 kB; -mem 12 -sndspeed 11025: 10.1 fps, majflt 2,134, VmSwap 12,172 kB; -mem 14 -sndspeed 22050: 8.1 fps, majflt 4,440, VmSwap 14,504 kB; -mem 10 -sndspeed 11025 in flight. The three 'td--mem-*' runs before them were mis-invoked (label '-mem', args reordered to '-sndspeed 11025 12 sr11k') and died with 'Error: Allocation of 268435456 byte heap failed' - the 256 MB default heap cannot be malloc'ed on this board, so any run without a well-formed -mem is a non-result. Comparison point: the old tiopex build (0.62 engine, SDL 1.2, forced 11 kHz device) read 19.5-21.6 fps at 11 kHz, so on stock 0.71 the rate/heap levers bought 8.0 -> 10.1 (+26%) and the remaining ~2x is not in the memory/sound subsystem.
facts.evidence: artifacts/quake/td-tyr071-2-020026/run.log; artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041/run.log; artifacts/quake/td-sr22k14-060630/run.log; artifacts/quake/td--mem-054943/run.log ('Error: Allocation of 268435456 byte heap failed'); scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh:32-34 (L=$1; ARGS=$*); docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:309-310

levers.lever: Launch with -sndspeed 11025 (menu.conf Exec line) - the app's own documented switch, so the app EXPLICITLY supports it; it changes the mixing rate at the source instead of via a capped device.
levers.why: Every sound in the shareware set is 11025 Hz 8-bit; at 11025 ResampleSfx is a 1:1 copy, the FIR filter and its pad are skipped (snd_mem.c:351,464), the cache set falls from 7.09 MB to 1.63 MB (4.34x), shm->buf from 64 kB to 16 kB, the mixer does 4.35x fewer sample-frames, and the sink (I2S mask has 11025) needs no plug resampling.
levers.expected_effect: Measured on the board already: 8.0 fps (48k, -mem 20) -> 10.1 fps (11025, -mem 12), majflt 6,601 -> 2,134, VmSwap 18.3 -> 12.2 MB. Estimated further headroom from the mixer alone is small (1-3% of the core); the win is memory.
levers.evidence: man/tyrquake.6 '-sndspeed n'; snd_sdl.c:79-81; scratchpad/q/pak.py totals; artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041/run.log vs td-tyr071-2-020026/run.log; esp32s31-i2s.c:520-523

levers.lever: Size -mem to the map+cache, not to a guess: for real play (server running) use -mem 21 at 11025 / 23 at 22050 / 26 at 48000 (rv32 estimates: play hunk ~16.9 MB + cache set 3.5/5.1/8.9 MB); for the timedemo alone 12/14/18 suffice. -mem 20 at any rate leaves only ~3.1 MB for the cache in play and thrashes sounds and models through the SD/resample/filter path on every miss.
levers.why: The heap is one lazily committed malloc and the cache is written only as it fills, so a larger -mem is free until used, while a too-small one turns every sound start into a pak read + resample (+64-tap FIR above 11025). The 8.5 MB item that made -mem 13/16 fail is the 8192-edict table, which no rate change touches.
levers.expected_effect: Removes cache thrash in play (host e1m1/48k at -mem 20 kept 32 of 165 cache entries; at 11k 141). No timedemo fps change expected at 11025 beyond -mem 12; play smoothness and level-load hitching are what improve. Must be verified by ear/feel on the board, and VmSwap will grow by exactly the extra cache actually used.
levers.evidence: scratchpad/runmap1.out, runmap3.out (REMAINING 2.73/2.82 MB, cache entries 32/141); zone.c:1263-1277; sys_unix.c:371-372; the -mem arithmetic in facts

levers.lever: Drop -zone to what is used (e.g. -zone 32) on the Exec line; documented switch, saves ~224 kB of memset (touched) hunk.
levers.why: Memory_Init allocates and zeroes zonesize (256 kB default) up front (zone.c:1291-1320, Hunk_AllocName memsets); the host run used 10,640 B in 231 blocks over the whole demo. Tiny, but it is a touched page cost on a 15 MB board and costs nothing.
levers.expected_effect: ~55 pages fewer resident/swapped. Not measurable in fps; recorded so it is not re-proposed as bigger than it is.
levers.evidence: common/zone.c:1291-1320; scratchpad/run48000.out 'zone print': 10640 bytes used in 231 blocks; man/tyrquake.6 '-zone'

levers.lever: Do NOT use a rate-capped ALSA device (s31route max_rate / s31route_11k) for TyrQuake, and keep 'default' at max_rate 48000.
levers.why: SDL_OpenAudio with an obtained spec accepts any granted rate (SDL_audio.c:1589, :1445-1450) and TyrQuake mixes at obtained.freq (snd_sdl.c:165), so a capped device forces the rate behind the app's back - the exact rule violation. -sndspeed achieves the same rate with the app's consent.
levers.expected_effect: No fps change versus -sndspeed 11025 (both end at shm->speed 11025); it only changes which side chose the rate.
levers.evidence: rootfs/s31route.c:531-546 (comment documents the mechanism); docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:301-312 (rule and withdrawn arm)

levers.lever: snd_filterquality 0 (cvar) at 22050/48000 to skip the 64-tap FIR and its pad; loadas8bit, _snd_mixahead, precache 0 - all app cvars.
levers.why: They are app-supported (registered cvars, snd_dma.c:195-206) and the computed task calls documented cvars legal, but the user's HARD RULES forbid 'config steering of the app for performance', and at 11025 the filter is already skipped, so the only rate where it would matter is one the memory arithmetic rules out anyway. loadas8bit is inert (all sounds 8-bit; allocation uses info->width). precache 0 would move every load to first play - worse.
levers.expected_effect: At 48 kHz: ~5 s less map-load CPU and ~5.9 kB less cache pad; zero at 11025. Not recommended; listed so it is not re-proposed.
levers.evidence: common/snd_mem.c:178,344-389,464-468; common/snd_dma.c:97,252-255; task HARD RULES text

levers.lever: Platform-side: nothing in the kernel/plugin can shrink the app's touched heap - Hunk_AllocName memsets (zone.c:618-624) and the cache fills by use - but zero-filled pages (edicts beyond ~600 used, 4.3 MB of net/console buffers, cl_entities/sv memsets) are already free on reclaim because the 7.1 swap zeromap never writes zero folios (perf-review item 41). Do not re-propose zram same_pages for this (perf-review items 2 and 41 closed it).
levers.why: Records why the 22.9 MB VmRSS+VmSwap at -mem 20 is mostly harmless zero pages after the first reclaim pass, and why the steady-state cost is the live cache + world, not the headline swap number.
levers.expected_effect: None to apply; prevents a repeat of the zram detour.
levers.evidence: docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:391,430; common/zone.c:618-624; NQ/cl_main.c:125-126; NQ/host.c:480

open_questions: Where does the remaining 2x go on stock 0.71 versus the 0.62 tiopex build at the same 11025 Hz (10.1 vs 19.5-21.6 fps)? It is not memory/sound: same cache set, majflt 2,134. Candidates outside this subsystem: SDL2 32-bpp software-renderer present path (VID_Update converts 8->32 per frame, vid_sdl.c:457-483, then SDL_RenderCopy/Present with vid_vsync=1 -> PRESENTVSYNC, vid_sdl.c:234-246), the 0.71 renderer's alpha/translucency and model lerp paths (r_lerpmodels default 1, r_alias.c:65), and the -bpp/vid_bpp 32 default (vid_mode.c:61) - the mode list's bpp is whatever the shim's visual advertises.

Exact rv32 hunk numbers for e1m1 in play: the host figures are 64-bit (world 2,461,520; edicts 8,650,768 -> 8,552,448 on rv32 by arithmetic). A board-side 'hunk print' after 'map e1m1' (console command, documented) would replace the ~16.9 MB / ~17.8 MB estimates; it needs the board, which is off limits right now.

The '-mem 13 and 16 fail' claim in perf-plan:292-293 and menu.conf:23-24 has no log in artifacts (grep for 'failed on'/'Hunk_AllocName_Raw' finds only the 09-11 doc table). Was it observed in play (map load, which the edict arithmetic explains) or in the timedemo (which the arithmetic says should run at 13)?

The in-flight -mem 10 -sndspeed 11025 arm (td-sr11k10-061251) sits below the estimated 11.7 MB timedemo need (8.2 hunk + 3.5 cache): expect cache eviction/reload during the demo and a worse number than -mem 12, which would confirm the cache-set arithmetic from the other side.

Number of simultaneously active mixer channels during demo1 (N in the 22+10N estimate) was not measured; snd_show 1 prints it per frame if anyone wants the mixer figure tightened - it is bounded at 1-3% of the core either way.

Does 'quit' via +exec on the board exit cleanly? On the host with SDL dummy drivers the process idled after the dump instead of exiting; irrelevant to the board harness (it kills by PID) but worth knowing before scripting console dumps there.

routes.title: Honest baseline on the launcher Exec line: -sndspeed 11025 -mem 10 (the app's own documented switches), harness window widened, Timedemo entry matched to -fullscreen
routes.steps: 1) menu.conf Quake block (overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf:26-28): add '-sndspeed 11025' to all three Exec lines; '-mem 10' for the Timedemo entry (no server, hunk ~8.2 MB + 3.5 MB cache set), and for play keep a larger heap because the server's 8192-edict table (sv_main.c:1355-1356, ~1,044 B x 8192 = 8.55 MB on rv32) is what fails at -mem 13/16, not the sound cache - estimate -mem 21 at 11025 and verify with the app's own 'hunk print' after 'map e1m1' on the board. 2) Timedemo entry -window -> -fullscreen so the menu path is the harness path (quake-timedemo.sh:44 launches -fullscreen; windowed presents go through LVGL compositing, lvdesk.c:5645-5662). 3) quake-timedemo.sh:71 runsh window 240/170 -> ~300/230: the first 0.71 run was killed by the board-side watchdog at 237 s (td-tyr071-1-015209) because 50 s boot + 121 s demo + settle exceeds it at 8 fps. 4) Add 'uname -a' to the generated run.sh: no tyr-quake artifact records the kernel build number. 5) Do NOT use 22050: measured 8.1 fps (td-sr22k14), no better than 48 kHz - the 64-tap FIR (snd_mem.c:344-389), the plug resample (I2S sink has no 22050, esp32s31-i2s.c:520-523) and the 3.1 MB cache eat the reduction.
routes.rule_argument: '-sndspeed n' and '-mem n' are documented in man/tyrquake.6 and honoured at snd_sdl.c:79-81 / zone.c:1266-1281; the user's audio clause (never-force-audio-rate, 2026-09-23, repeated in the task) says an option the app itself documents counts as supported, and the rate is then chosen by the app, not by a capped device (the s31route_11k arm was the violation). Unresolved tension to surface, not decide: the 2026-09-20 ruling that steering an app to a cheaper config is 'still cheating' has no explicit TyrQuake ruling; the in-flight measurements and the computed task both assume -sndspeed is legal. No cvars, no capped device, no AUDIODEV.
routes.expected_fps: MEASURED, not estimated: 10.7 fps at -mem 10 / 11025 (969 frames, 90.9 s, td-sr11k10-061251), 10.1 at -mem 12 / 11025 (td-sr11k12-060041), 8.1 at -mem 14 / 22050, 8.0 at -mem 20 / 48000. This is the base every other route multiplies. It does not reach 20 on its own.
routes.arithmetic: 48k -> 11k took 8.0 -> 10.7 (+34%): majflt 6,601 -> 2,300, VmSwap 18.3 -> 10.0 MB, demo wall 120.9 -> 90.9 s. Paging tax at 10.7: 2,300 majflt x ~3.3 ms = 7.6 s = 8.3% of wall (estimate; per-fault cost from current-state 2036-2044). Frame budget: 93.5 ms/frame vs tiopex 0.62/SDL1.2 at the same rate and heap ~48 ms (19.2-21.6 fps) - a 45 ms/frame gap of which the platform can see at most: SDL2 same-size blit 3.1-12 ms (accel-plan), viewsize default 110 vs tiopex's 100 (0.71 screen.c:200 vs sdlquake screen.c:115 -> sb_lines 24 vs 48 -> 320x216 vs 320x192 raster, +12.5% pixels, ~3 ms, app default, not steerable), paging delta ~3-5 ms, leaving ~20-27 ms/frame inside the stock 0.71 engine/SDL2 that no profile has attributed. OVERALL VERDICT: 20 fps = 50 ms/frame needs -43.5 ms; routes R2-R6 compound to 10.7 x 1.10-1.49 = 11.8-15.9 fps (estimate, all arithmetic in each route). 20 fps on stock 0.71 is not reachable by platform levers unless the R3 profile shows the unattributed residual is platform-visible (bus contention/reclaim), or the user re-rules the app-side items in R8.
routes.evidence: artifacts/quake/td-sr11k10-061251/run.log, td-sr11k12-060041/run.log, td-sr22k14-060630/run.log, td-tyr071-2-020026/run.log, td-tyr071-1-015209/run.log (RS_TIMEKILL at 237 s); tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/man/tyrquake.6 (-sndspeed, -mem); common/snd_sdl.c:35,79-81,165; common/zone.c:1266-1281; NQ/sv_main.c:1355-1356 + include/progs.h:37-50 (edict table); common/screen.c:200,717-722 vs tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/screen.c:115,601-605 (viewsize/sb_lines); scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh:33-34,44,71; overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf:19-28; docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md log 2026-09-23 HARD RULE entry; linux-71-port/sound/soc/espressif/esp32s31-i2s.c:520-523
routes.cheapest_test: Already measured. One more fresh boot at -mem 10/11025 to establish the spread (the per-boot lottery is +-10% on Quake). For play: one board session 'map e1m1' then 'hunk print' at -mem 21 (both app console commands) to replace the rv32 edict estimate. <10 min.
routes.effort: 30 minutes of edits (menu.conf, quake-timedemo.sh); no build, no flash.
routes.risks: -mem 10 fails at map load in real play (edict table + progs + world ~16.9 MB, estimate), so timedemo and play Exec lines differ; the 'config steering' ruling is unresolved for TyrQuake; kernel build number of the four runs is presumed #363 but not recorded in the artifacts.

routes.title: Build stock 0.71 with its Makefile's DEFAULT Linux video/input target (X11) instead of the 'experimental' SDL one, and complete our X server for it: ShmCompletion, XShmGetEventBase, an Xxf86vm client shim
routes.steps: 1) rootfs/build-tyrquake.sh, a second product: drop USE_SDL=Y (Makefile:18 'New (experimental) SDL video/sound/input targets'); TARGET_OS=UNIX TARGET_UNIX=linux then defaults VID_TARGET=x11 IN_TARGET=x11 (Makefile:118-120); set SND_TARGET=sdl because the linux default is pulseaudio (Makefile:133-136) and oss asks 48000 first too (snd_oss.c:41) - snd_sdl.c is the same file, -sndspeed still applies; links X11 Xext Xxf86vm (Makefile:936-939); put XShm.h/xf86vmode.h protocol headers in staging (host headers, not app changes). 2) xshim: advertise a MIT-SHM first_event (xshim.c:6206-6211 returns 0: 'we never ShmCompletion, and nothing asks us to') and send the ShmCompletion event after the copy when send_event=1 - vid_x.c:1042-1052 passes True and spins in VID_ProcessEvents until oktodraw (vid_x.c:963-964), so without it the client hangs. 3) xstubs: forward XShmGetEventBase (xstubs.c:163-212 forwards only QueryExtension/QueryVersion/CreateImage/Attach/Detach/PutImage); xlite: return the advertised base. 4) libXxf86vm.so.1 shim in xlite/ modelled on xlite/randr/xrandr.c (549 lines): QueryVersion, GetModeLine, GetAllModeLines, SwitchToMode, SetViewPort over xshim's existing VidMode minors 0/1/6/10/12 (xshim.c:8028-8087). A symbol diff of vid_x.c+in_x11.c+x11_core.c+vid_x11_common.c against images/xlite-exports.txt + xstubs shows exactly these five plus XShmGetEventBase missing (XLateKey is the app's own). 5) Deploy to /root/quake on SD; Exec line as R1 (fullscreen: in_x11.c grabs automatically when VID_IsFullScreen(), in_x11.c:502-512).
routes.rule_argument: It is the app's own build system selecting its own default target: readme.txt:36-38 documents choosing targets by Makefile variables, and the existing script already sets TARGET_OS/TARGET_UNIX/USE_SDL/USE_X86_ASM/CD_TARGET the same way (build-tyrquake.sh:19-23). No source patch, no define, no custom library in the app: X11/Xext/Xxf86vm are the platform's X client libraries (xlite/xstubs already stand in for libX11/libXext/libXrandr). All new code is in xshim/xlite/xstubs. FLAG for the orchestrator: this is a build-target choice rather than a platform change, one step further than the accepted script only in omitting USE_SDL=Y; also -std=gnu11 stays required (GCC 14 C23 default).
routes.expected_fps: 11.1-12.3 fps (+3-15%), ESTIMATE. Ceiling unknown until R3's profile shows SDL2's per-frame share beyond the blit.
routes.arithmetic: SDL2 client critical path per 320x240 frame: expand 76.8 kB read + 153.6 kB write into the texture (vid_sdl.c:466-476), then SDL_RenderCopy's same-size SDL_BlitSurface texture -> MIT-SHM segment 153.6 kB read + 153.6 kB write (SDL_render_sw.c:802-803, SW_RenderPresent 964-971), then xshim's 153.6 kB copy before the reply. X11 target: vid_x.c renders 8-bit into the SHM image rows and st2_fixup expands 8->16 IN PLACE (vid_x.c:279-284, vid.buffer = framebuffer data at :481/1022), then XShmPutImage - the SDL blit is gone. That copy is measured at exactly this size: 3.09 ms quiet / 11.98 ms loaded (accel-plan.md cost table, 320x240 153600 row). 93.5 ms -> 90.4 ms (11.1 fps) quiet, -> 81.5 ms (12.3 fps) loaded. Not counted: SDL2 renderer/command-queue/event-pump overhead per frame (unmeasured; the sdl2-indexed-timers canary at 22.5-27.5 ms vs sdl1-indexed 8.55-14.7 ms per frame bounds the whole SDL2 present path at ~10-14 ms on a heavier ARGB variant). Memory: two SHM segments 307 kB vs SDL2's texture + segment 307 kB, a wash.
