routes.cheapest_test: QUAKE_BIN=./tyr-quake-x11 scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh x11 -mem 10 -sndspeed 11025 (fresh boot, ~4 min). Kill criteria: no 'fullscreen 320x240' in /var/log/lvdesk.log or fps <= 10.7 on two boots. Mouse: 30 s play with XLITE_TRACE_INPUT=1 and a uinject drag - expect MotionNotify + recentring warps; ear-check sound.
routes.effort: 1-2 days: Xxf86vm shim ~250 lines, xshim ShmCompletion ~40 lines, xstubs/xlite ~20 lines, staging headers, build script line; one xip rebuild for the shim (or SD-side .so for the test).
routes.risks: Default visual must be 16 bpp (xlite advertises 16; a 24-depth default takes st3_fixup with pixel_width 4); override_redirect fullscreen window + CWSaveUnder/CWBackingStore bits must be accepted by xshim; ShmCompletion event layout must match libXext's XShmCompletionEvent (xlite decodes it); per-motion recentring warps (in_x11.c:89-96 toggles PointerMotionMask around XWarpPointer) rely on xshim honouring the mask order or the client sees a zero-offset motion it ignores; the unattributed ~20-27 ms/frame residual is untouched, so this route alone caps near 12 fps.

routes.title: The pre-reply/post-reply copy family for a fullscreen 16-bit SHM client, measured on THIS client first (NOSYNCWAIT bound, no row hashing, PC profile), then xshim lands ShmPutImage directly in kms_fs_map and issues DIRTYFB
routes.steps: Measure (no build): a) same-boot A/B/A XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT=1 vs off (xlite.c:1002-1014; PRE='export XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT=1' reaches the setsid'd process), A-to-A gap as the error bar - the ceiling of the whole family on this client; b) XSHIM_NOROWDMG=1 (xshim.c:614-624) A/B; c) XSHIM_PROF=1 (xshim.c:2777,9447) for the ShmPutImage minor's ns; d) scripts/board/profile-apps.sh PC samples on tyr-quake at -mem 10/11025, resolved with h1s-report.py --symdir against nm -nS rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg and images/libSDL2-2.0.so.0.3200.10: VID_Update expand vs SDL_BlitCopy vs XSync wait vs engine - the number that attributes the 45 ms/frame gap. Build only if (a) reads > 3%: xshim's fullscreen 16-bit ShmPutImage copies into the mode's dumb buffer (kms_fs_map) instead of d->buf->px, skips the FNV row hash (xshim.c:5510-5548), and issues DRM_IOCTL_MODE_DIRTYFB itself (kms.c:757-776) or hands lvdesk the rect - deleting lvdesk's second 153.6 kB memcpy (lvdesk.c:4856-4858).
routes.rule_argument: All in xshim/xlite/lvdesk/kernel (ours). NOSYNCWAIT itself is a bound, not a shippable default: the client gets no completion guarantee and an lvdesk stall longer than one frame tears; MIT-SHM adoption stays closed (xshim.c:5420-5450, dead-end #15). Not the C89/X3-11 SDL patches.
routes.expected_fps: 11.1-11.5 fps (+4-8%) ESTIMATE if the bus argument holds; 0% if the NOSYNCWAIT bound reads inside the A-A gap (then close the family for SDL2 too).
routes.arithmetic: The review's T2.7 argument (post-reply work on the 63.7%-idle CPU1 is 0% on client fps 'by construction', perf-review:219-221) assumes CPU isolation. The accel-plan measures the same 153,600 B memcpy at 3.09 ms quiet vs 11.98 ms with concurrent traffic ('PSRAM bandwidth is the ceiling for both', CPU 'degrades 3.9x'), and per frame the bus also carries lvdesk's 153.6 kB read + 153.6 kB write, the PPA's 153.6 kB read + 614 kB write (640x480x2), and the LCD scanout's 768,000 B x 42 Hz = 32 MB/s continuous. Hash: 38,400 xor+mul on the critical path = 0.3-0.6 ms (estimate). lvdesk copy off the bus: 307 kB/frame ~ 3-6 ms of bus time at 50-100 MB/s (estimate). 93.5 -> 87-90 ms. The measured ceiling is whatever (a) reads; the SDL1 canary closed this family at <= 2.5% (perf-plan:98-101) when the pre-reply work was two tiny requests, which is why it must be re-measured for a 153.6 kB pre-reply copy.
routes.evidence: docs/accel-plan.md cost model table and points 1-3; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:219-221 (T2.7), 162-168 (C94/X3-11), dead-ends #7,#10,#15; docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:98-101 (NOSYNCWAIT closed on SDL1); lvdesk/xshim.c:614-624,5420-5450,5496-5548,9633-9638; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:4856-4868; lvdesk/kms.c:757-776; xlite/xlite.c:1002-1014; scripts/board/profile-apps.sh, h1s-report.py; memory s31-cache-counters (2.1 M/s shared-D-cache conflicts under Quake); docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:209-211 (CPU1 63.7% idle)
routes.cheapest_test: Three quake-timedemo.sh runs in one boot are not possible (fresh boot per run); use a same-boot A/B/A of ~40 s demo windows with the harness's PRE hook and a shortened +timedemo, or three fresh boots (12 min). Then one profile-apps.sh capture (10 min). Kill: NOSYNCWAIT delta inside the A-A gap.
routes.effort: Measurements 1-2 hours. Build 1 day (xshim + lvdesk), one xip image rebuild.
routes.risks: Dumb-buffer mapping is cached (dead-end #10) but write-combining-sensitive (lvdesk.c:4863-4868 'PAIR THE STORES'); the client's next ShmPutImage can race the PPA's read of kms_fs_map unless the scanout stays double-buffered; the h1s sampler's 1 kHz/100 Hz phase lock (review C09) biases kernel shares; the board cannot be touched until the in-flight measurement ends.

routes.title: Ship the 360 MHz CPU clock (proven real, memtest-clean, radios in band, not shipped)
routes.steps: bootloader/main/s31_oc.h:9 S31_CPU_OC_MHZ 0 -> 360 (main.c:400-463 does the esp_pm + XTAL-detour switch); apply the vendor patch (clk_tree_ll.h 'case 360: fb_div 9', rtc_clk.c dividers mem 2 / sys 4 / apb 2) from the Makefile on EVERY loader build because the container's /opt/esp-idf is pristine per run (today only scripts/board/build-oc.sh:38-55 does it ad hoc; no Makefile hook exists); esp32s31.dtsi timebase-frequency and opensbi S31_TIMEBASE_HZ -> 360000000 (make linux AND make opensbi); flash with scripts/board/flash-trio.sh and its host/board ratio test (~1.000); then the soak the plan names as the gate and that has never run: one hour at 360 of memtest loops, Doom, the desktop and radios.
routes.rule_argument: Platform only (loader, DTS, OpenSBI). The plan records it as 'the user's call': the memory domain runs 180 MHz against a vendor ceiling of 160, permanently, on the only board.
routes.expected_fps: 11.0-12.0 fps (+3-12%) ESTIMATE from a measured +3-4% on tiopex; the upper end only if the SDL2 client is bandwidth-bound.
routes.arithmetic: Measured on tiopex at 11 kHz: 20.9/19.2/20.0/19.4 (median 19.7) vs 19.2-19.4 at 320 = +3-4%, not the +9% the 240 MHz mirror slope (0.72) predicted, because PSRAM stays on MPLL. But 360 also moves the memory domain 160 -> 180 (+12.5%); if R3 shows the 0.71/SDL2 frame is bus-bound its gain could approach the clock ratio. 10.7 x 1.03 = 11.0; x 1.125 = 12.0. At the 48 kHz swap-backed point less (fault service does not scale with the core).
routes.evidence: docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md Phase 5 (all checkboxes and the ship-decision text); log entries '360 MHz WORKS (try 4, #351)', '360 MHz, four boots', '360 MHz radios: no degradation'; scripts/board/build-oc.sh:1-60; scripts/board/flash-trio.sh; bootloader/main/s31_oc.h; bootloader/main/main.c:400-463; bootloader/sdkconfig:2686; memory s31-cpu-overclock, overclock-verify-radios
routes.cheapest_test: flash-trio.sh images/oc360 + ratio test, then ONE quake-timedemo.sh run at -mem 10/-sndspeed 11025 (~15 min total), then restore the 320 trio via flash-trio.sh. Kill: ratio != ~1.000, memtest mismatch, or fps within the +-10% lottery on two boots.
routes.effort: Half a day for the Makefile hook and trio; one hour soak; the ship decision is the user's.
routes.risks: Silent PSRAM corruption class (memory domain 12.5% over spec); radios measured n=2 only (~10% lower throughput, inside the band); 400 MHz is priced at ~+5% and only after 360 soaks clean.

routes.title: Return RAM in the 10-12 MB-swap regime (udevd off, .text..fast cold trim, s31-bt MCL_CURRENT, min_free_kbytes 512), judged on majflt and SDSTAT, not fps
routes.steps: 1) C51: remove S10udevd (do not substitute mdev); verify USB/BT hotplug and that nothing reads /run/udev; ~240 kB anon+tmpfs certain. 2) Re-resolve the 235,520 B .text..fast against the #363 map and drop objects with zero samples from S31_FAST_OBJS (pre-DCE figure 180-220 kB cold); gate on same-hart pingpong, because layout moves alone swing it +-15%. 3) s31-bt: drop mlockall(MCL_CURRENT), keep the per-buffer mlock of the audio path (s31-bt.c:1570-1591); ear-test A2DP afterwards; 100-200 kB estimate. 4) vm.min_free_kbytes 1024 -> 512 (99-s31-memory.conf:17): +744 kB MemAvailable measured idle, sign uncertain under swap - fresh-boot pair on the -mem 10 arm. 5) Optional arm: vm.page-cluster 2 -> 3 in physical-slot mode, judged on /sys/block/mmcblk0/stat fields 1 and 3 (the -mem 20 run averaged 11.4 KiB per read, so cluster 2 already merges ~3 slots). NOT libasound into XIP: 943,548 B against ~780 kB free across the two images (Makefile:930-931 comment; perf-plan:167) - it does not fit unless something leaves.
routes.rule_argument: Platform placement and kernel knobs; Bluetooth stays fully enabled (only a lock scope changes); slab is not touched (closed); zram stays rejected (dead-end #2, s31-swap.conf). udevd removal is the review's C51 verdict 'remove, do not replace'.
routes.expected_fps: 11.0-11.1 fps (+3-4%) ESTIMATE, plus unmeasured kswapd relief.
routes.arithmetic: MemAvailable during the -mem 10 run was 432 kB with 2,300 majflt (VmSwap 10.0 MB); tiopex at the same heap and rate took 785-1,352. Returning ~0.6-1.3 MB (240 + 150-200 + 100-200 + up to 744) plausibly brings faults to the tiopex band: (800-1,100 fewer) x ~3.3 ms = 2.6-3.6 s of 90.9 s = +3-4%. page-cluster 3: 8 slots per request cost 2.49 + 32/48 = 3.16 ms vs ~2.73 ms for 11 KiB; needs ~75% hit rate to break even at 432 kB free (review: 30-40% regression chance).
routes.evidence: artifacts/quake/td-sr11k10-061251/run.log (MEM/QUAKE/SDSTAT lines); docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:157-159 (T2.3), 178 (C51), 213-216,287 (X1-11a), 245, 319 (C50); docs/current-state.md:4915-4920, 6541-6556; rootfs/s31-bt.c:1570-1591,2121-2139; overlay/etc/sysctl.d/99-s31-memory.conf:17,93-99; overlay/etc/init.d/S10udevd:31-63; images/System.map __text_fast_start/__text_fast_end; Makefile:920-931; docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:167 (~780 kB XIP slack); overlay/etc/s31-swap.conf (four zram rejections)
routes.cheapest_test: Two fresh boots with PRE='sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=512' vs shipped, judged on majflt/SDSTAT/MemAvailable (8 min); one boot with S10udevd disabled plus a mouse hot-unplug/replug; pingpong medians for the .text..fast trim. Kill: majflt not down by > the boot-to-boot spread.
routes.effort: Half a day for the sysctl/udevd arms; one kernel build for the .text..fast trim; s31-bt one rebuild and an ear test.
routes.risks: min_free 512 can move reclaim into the fault path (Run D was confounded with swappiness 0); udevd semantics for hotplug/uhid (CONFIG_UHID is off anyway); page-cluster 3 evicts a resident page per speculative one at 432 kB free.

routes.title: libc-side double math (C86) and, pending a ruling, the s31fp LD_PRELOAD on the Exec line
routes.steps: C86 (platform library): musl arch overrides in the crosstool libc - floor/ceil/trunc/round/modf by integer bit manipulation (bit-exact), sinf/cosf/atan2f in single precision with fmadd.s (musl's float trig is double inside: images/libc.nm has __sindf/__cosdf/__rem_pio2f), and s31fp's __muldf3/__adddf3/conv linked into libc.so ahead of libgcc; gated first on an LD_PRELOAD caller census of tyr-quake. Separately: LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libs31fp.so on the Exec line (rootfs/s31fp/preload.c patches the app's own statically linked libgcc helpers by byte signature in a private COW page; all 9 signatures match rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg today) ONLY if the user rules it platform - the review's history lens called exactly that the C87 redline route (perf-review:367) while the task text calls it platform.
routes.rule_argument: libc.so is a Buildroot/crosstool-built shared library the app loads dynamically - platform by every rule statement; no relink, no app flag. The preload half is the open ruling: it rewrites bytes of the app's own text at load time, which the memory note s31-never-rebuild-client-apps and perf-review:367 read as the redline even though the file on disk is untouched.
routes.expected_fps: 10.8-11.0 fps (+1-3%) ESTIMATE; the preload alone ~+1%.
routes.arithmetic: Only profile is tiopex 0.62 (h1s-062518, 12,000 samples): __adddf3 201 + __muldf3 94 + __subdf3 60 + __truncdfsf2 25 = 380 = 3.17% of CPU0, libm bodies 0.91%, absolute ceiling 4.17%; 0.71's static call-site census is the same footprint (111 muldf3 / 83 adddf3 / 70 subdf3 / 199 extendsfdf2 sites, none in D_DrawSpans8). Preload: adddf3+subdf3 261 x (1-1/1.4) + muldf3 94 x (1-1/2.5) = 131 samples = 1.1% of CPU0 -> fps 1/(0.86/1.011+0.14)-1 = +0.9%. C86 realistic +1.2-3.5% of CPU0 (review T1.7) -> +1-3% fps. Below the per-boot band; validate on same-boot A/B/A or bundle.
routes.evidence: docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:96-104 (T1.7/C86), 367 (C87); rootfs/s31fp/preload.c, sigs.h, build.sh; docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:525-541 (mul 738 -> 296 ns, add/sub 423 -> 308 ns; 'built, verified, NOT enabled'); images/libc.nm; tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/mathlib.c:317-324,551-577; NQ/host.c:64-66; memory s31-soft-double-cost, s31-hardware-float
routes.cheapest_test: PRE='export LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libs31fp.so' vs off, same-boot A/B/A of a shortened demo (needs the ruling first); caller census via the preload's own trace. Kill: delta inside the A-A gap.
routes.effort: Minutes for the preload arm; days for C86 (musl overrides + toolchain rebuild + bit-exactness tests).
routes.risks: Trig overrides are <= 1 ulp, not bit-identical; preload.c does not patch objects dlopen()ed after its constructor; the C87 ruling.

routes.title: Library codegen: rebuild the Buildroot libraries/libc with Zcb+Zcmp, or libSDL2 at -O2 - NOT recommended without a profile
routes.steps: Only if R3's profile shows libSDL2/libc above ~5% of the frame: add zcb_zcmp to BR2_RISCV_ISA_EXTRA, BR2_TARGET_OPTIMIZATION and CT_ARCH_ARCH, rebuild toolchain + rootfs; or a per-package SDL2 CFLAGS override to -O2.
routes.rule_argument: Platform libraries. RULE RISK: tyr-quake takes its -march from the Buildroot wrapper (toolchain-wrapper.c:390-401), so a toolchain-default change silently changes the stock app's codegen unless the app build pins today's -march - which is itself a build flag; that needs a ruling before any toolchain rebuild. libSDL2 is Buildroot-built; -O2 vs -Os is a package flag, not an SDL patch.
routes.expected_fps: <= +0.5% ESTIMATE; 0 to negative for -O2.
routes.arithmetic: Kernel Zcmp/Zcb bought +2-3% on a ~40% kernel share (~0.06 fps-% per share point); libraries are ~8% of a tiopex frame (934/12,000 samples) of which 4.2% is call-bound libc math -> ~+0.5% at best. The kernel's selective -O2 arm measured nothing (#355, 19.5 vs 19.5, +32.8 kB) and -msave-restore alone regressed (#341, 17.7 vs 19.1).
routes.evidence: docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md Phase 3b ('Zcb+Zcmp SHIPS (#353)', '-msave-restore MEASURED WORSE', 'Selective -O2 (#355): CLOSED'); docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:284 (C38), 337; buildroot-external/configs/esp32s31_rootfs_defconfig:11,24; configs/riscv32-esp-linux-musl.config:28,43; Makefile:26-38,919-926; artifacts/quake/h1s-062518 split
routes.cheapest_test: None until the profile exists; the R3 profile is the gate.
routes.effort: A full toolchain + rootfs rebuild (hours) for the ISA change; a package rebuild for -O2.
routes.risks: Silently changes the stock app's codegen (rule); not resolvable on fps; the SDL2 share is unmeasured.

routes.title: Closed or forbidden levers, listed so they are not re-proposed (app-side items that WOULD move fps but break the rules, and platform items already measured null)
routes.steps: Do not: set viewsize 100 / snd_filterquality / loadas8bit / _snd_mixahead / vid_vsync / -surfcachesize / -particles / d_mipcap (app config steering - even though viewsize 100 alone would match tiopex's 320x192 raster and is worth ~6% by pixel count, estimate); use a capped ALSA device or AUDIODEV steering; patch SDL2's software renderer (C89) or musl-in-app; put tyr-quake or its data in XIP flash (no-apps-in-flash; measured 10.7 vs 10.9 anyway); -O3/-funroll-loops (died twice); SDL_VIDEO_X11_WINDOW_VISUALID 32-bit (chocolate-doom 10.7 -> 5.5); MIT-SHM segment adoption (31.7 fps, flickers, illegal); zram (rejected four times); swappiness 0 (OOM-kills Quake); reclaim slab (closed); disable Bluetooth/Wi-Fi; PPA/GDMA for the ShmPutImage copy (SysV segment is not PPA-addressable, xshim.c:194-197); kernel text placement arms (spine in RAM, HRTICK, touch poll, prelock, hot-first packing - all null or negative).
routes.rule_argument: Each is an explicit recorded rejection: the app redline (2026-09-20), the audio hard rule (2026-09-23), no-apps-in-flash (2026-09-22), CLAUDE.md standing constraints, perf-review dead-ends #2, #11, #15, #20, #81, and the Phase 1-4 log entries. The only app-side item worth a user re-ruling is viewsize/cvars, because the 0.71 defaults (viewsize 110, r_lerpmodels 1, snd_filterquality 3) are part of why stock 0.71 is slower than the 0.62 glue build at the same rate.
routes.expected_fps: Not applicable (forbidden or measured null). For the record: forced 11 kHz device was +35-50% on tiopex - exactly why it must not be a baseline.
routes.arithmetic: viewsize 110 vs 100: sb_lines 24 vs 48 -> 3D raster 320x216 vs 320x192 = +12.5% pixels; at ~50% of the frame in rasterisation (0.62 profile user share 50.9%) that is ~6% of frame time - an app default, not a platform lever.
routes.evidence: memory notes s31-never-rebuild-client-apps, never-force-audio-rate, no-apps-in-flash, s31-slab-is-not-a-lever; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:369,374,391,396-400,409,470 and dead-end table; docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md Phases 1-4 log; overlay/etc/s31-swap.conf; lvdesk/xshim.c:194-197,5420-5450; tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/screen.c:200,717-722; tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/screen.c:115,601-605; docs/current-state.md:7786-7788
routes.cheapest_test: None; closed by measurement or by rule.
routes.effort: None.
routes.risks: Re-proposing any of these has already cost days each (zram three eras, the forced-rate baseline, the XIP copy); the viewsize difference must be stated whenever 0.71 is compared to the tiopex numbers or the comparison is unfair to the platform.

routes.title: The bundle: app-documented rate/heap + stock X11 target + 360 MHz + RAM return + libc math - and the honest ceiling arithmetic
routes.steps: 1) Base: launch stock tyr-quake with its own documented switches '-sndspeed 11025 -mem 12' (menu.conf Exec lines 26-28; the harness already does this). 2) Build the stock X11 target (R4) and ship the xlite/xshim pieces it needs. 3) Ship 360 MHz after the soak (R5). 4) Return RAM under the game (R6). 5) C86 libc math (R7). 6) Only after the profile (R2) says the unattributed ~14 ms/frame is platform-side, chase it; if it is engine work, stop and report that 20 fps needs an app-side option.
routes.rule_argument: Every step is platform (kernel, loader, xlite, xshim, Buildroot libc) or the app's own documented command-line switches (man/tyrquake.6 '-sndspeed n', '-mem n'; snd_sdl.c:79-81; zone.c:1266-1281). The build-target variables VID_TARGET/IN_TARGET/SND_TARGET are the stock Makefile's own (Makefile:105-135, 934-1023), not defines or patches. Two items need the user's explicit ratification because the record is in tension: (a) '-sndspeed 11025' is allowed by the audio rule's wording ('an option the app itself documents') but the 2026-09-20 ruling calls steering an app to a cheaper config 'still cheating' (memory s31-never-rebuild-client-apps); (b) the s31fp LD_PRELOAD patches the app's own libgcc copies in a private COW page - the task calls it platform, the review calls it the redline route (perf-review:367).
routes.expected_fps: Realistic 12.0-13.2 fps (from 10.7). Optimistic ceiling 15.4 if the unattributed 14 ms/frame is entirely platform and fully removed; 19.2 only with zero paging on top of that. 20 fps is NOT reached by the sum of every within-rules lever at its most optimistic value; it needs either the profile to reveal a platform cost larger than any estimate here, or an app-side option (viewsize 100, R8) the rules forbid.
routes.arithmetic: Decomposition of the run of record (48 kHz, -mem 20): 120.9 s / 969 frames = 124.8 ms/frame. Paging (SD time, model 2.49 ms + size/48 MB/s, docs/current-state.md:2036-2044): reads 9,748-1,268 = 8,480 x 2.73 ms = 23.1 s, writes 1,983-97 = 1,886 x 2.7 ms = 5.1 s -> 28 s (23%, +-4 s: the boot baseline SDSTAT is from another boot). Present path (client critical, estimate from accel-plan.md copy table + dead-end #9 expander rates): expand 76,800 px x 49-66 ns = 3.8-5.1 ms + SDL_BlitCopy 153,600 B = 3.09 ms + xshim copy+hash >= 3.09 ms (blocks the client's XSync, xshim.c:9633-9638) + ~1 ms cross-hart wake = 11-12.3 ms x 969 = 10.7-11.9 s (9-10%). 48 kHz mixing 1-3% = 1.2-3.6 s; S_FilterSfx at load ~5 s (7.09 M samples x 64 taps / ~3.5 cycles at 320 MHz) and it IS inside the timed window (td_starttime is set on the frame that reads the serverinfo message, NQ/cl_demo.c:59-62, so map+sound load is timed). Kernel non-idle other (irq/sched/timers): no 0.71 profile; the 0.62 #338 profile's 31.5% scaled by the pingpong speed-up (542->335 us) ~ 20% = ~24 s (+-6). Engine user = remainder ~50 s (41%). AT 11 kHz (the new base, td-sr11k10/12): 90.9-95.6 s. Paging: -mem 10: 4,119 reads (68.1 MB, 16.6 KB avg -> 2.84 ms) = 11.7 s + 981 writes x 2.72 = 2.7 s = 14.4 s (15.8%); -mem 12: 3,385 reads (49.4 MB) = 9.4 s + 767 writes = 2.1 s = 11.5 s (12.0%). Present 10.7-11.9 s (12%). Mixing <1 s, filter 0 (snd_mem.c:351). Kernel ~18 s (+-5). Engine ~47 s (+-8) = 48.5 ms/frame. Tiopex 0.62 at 11 kHz on #363 (td-fastfn-hot-1/2): 44.9-45.6 s: paging 1,265 reads x 2.84 + 355 writes x 2.6 = 4.5 s, present ~2.4 s (76.8 kB memcpy + round trip), kernel ~9 s, engine ~29 s = 30 ms/frame. Engine delta ~18 ms/frame: viewsize default 110 vs 100 (0.71 screen.c:200 vs sdlquake screen.c:115) = 216 vs 192 3D rows, +12.5% of the rasteriser ~ +3.5 ms; r_lerpmodels <0.5 ms; ~14 ms/frame UNATTRIBUTED (needs R2). TARGET: 20 fps = 50.0 ms/frame, i.e. -43.8 ms from 93.8. Levers (realistic / optimistic, ms per frame): X11 target present -3.0 / -4.5; RAM return + cluster on paging -2 / -7; 360 MHz on the CPU-bound ~75% -2.5 / -6; C86+s31fp -0.8 / -1.5; xshim hash off -0.3 / -0.6. Sum -8.6 / -19.6 -> 85.2 / 74.2 ms = 11.7 / 13.5 fps. Compounded as fractions (1.035 x 1.03 x 1.03 x 1.015 x 1.005 = 1.12 realistic): 10.7 -> 12.0; optimistic 1.27 -> 13.6. Add the whole unattributed 14 ms as removable: 60-71 ms -> 14-16.6 fps. Add zero paging: 45-57 ms -> 17.5-22 fps only at the corner where every estimate breaks the right way. Error bars: per-boot spread 2-5% on a quiet harness (perf-plan 'Lottery CLOSED'), paging +-2 s from the cross-boot baseline, kernel share +-6 s, engine +-8 s.
routes.evidence: artifacts/quake/td-sr11k10-061251/run.log, td-sr11k12-060041/run.log, td-sr22k14-060630/run.log, td-tyr071-2-020026/run.log, td--mem-054943/run.log (SDSTAT baseline), td-fastfn-hot-1-202744 and -2-203215 (tiopex 21.3/21.6); docs/accel-plan.md:35-45 (153,600 B memcpy 3.09 ms quiet / 11.98 loaded); docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:398 (dead-end #9 expander ns/px), :219-221; NQ/cl_demo.c:53-62; common/screen.c:200 vs tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/screen.c:115; tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/Makefile:18,105-135,934-1023; man/tyrquake.6 '-sndspeed', '-mem'.
routes.cheapest_test: None on its own - it is the sum of R2-R7. The single test that decides whether R1 can ever reach 20 is R2 (one profiled fresh boot at -sndspeed 11025 -mem 12): if user-side engine+present time exceeds ~55 ms/frame there, no platform route reaches 50 ms/frame and this should be reported as the answer.
routes.effort: 3-6 days total (R4 1-2 days, R5 1 day + 1 h soak, R6 half a day, R7 days), plus 6-8 fresh boots of measurement.
routes.risks: The headline risk is the record: the review's own Quake ceiling arithmetic on tiopex ('20 fps not reliably reachable') was beaten by +7% from code-size work it under-priced 4x, so estimates here can be wrong in both directions; but the 0.71 engine term (~47 s of 91) is app code the rules forbid touching, and nothing platform-side scales it except the clock (+3-4% measured). Every item below the per-boot band must be bundled and judged on pingpong/majflt/SDSTAT, not fps alone.

routes.title: Gate measurement first: PC profile + present-path timers on stock 0.71 at 11 kHz (decides whether 20 is reachable)
routes.steps: On the next free board window, three fresh boots, each <= 10 min: (1) scripts/board/profile-apps.sh with APPS set to the tyr-quake timedemo line from artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041/run.sh (it saves /proc/<pid>/maps during capture); resolve with scripts/board/h1s-report.py images/System.map <pcs> --maps maps.txt --sym tyr-quake=<nm -nS rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg> --sym libSDL2-2.0.so.0.3200.10=<nm -nS of the unstripped SDL2> --sym libc.so=images/libc.nm. Read: VID_Update vs SDL_BlitCopy vs xlite XSync-wait vs D_DrawSpans8/R_GenerateSpans vs libc __*df* vs kernel irq/sched/timers, and per-thread CPU from /proc/<pid>/task/*/stat (audio thread). (2) Same run with XSHIM_PROF=1 in lvdesk's environment (xshim.c:9447) for ShmPutImage ns per request, and /proc/interrupts deltas over the demo (the 09-21 '74% kernel = wake-ups' finding was on SDL 1.2 at 48 kHz; the SDL2/11 kHz wake-up rate is unmeasured). (3) XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT=1 A/B/A same boot (xlite.c:1002-1046) as the bound on the whole pre-reply-copy + round-trip family for THIS client; report the A-to-A gap as the error bar.
routes.rule_argument: Pure measurement with existing instruments; nothing is shipped. XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT is a measurement knob, never a default (it races the compositor read; xlite.c:1002-1009).
routes.expected_fps: No fps change by itself. Output: the ~14 ms/frame unattributed term split into engine / present / kernel with sample counts, which sets the ceiling for R1: engine+present > 55 ms/frame at 11 kHz means 20 fps is unreachable within the rules.
routes.arithmetic: At 10.7 fps the frame is 93.8 ms; the estimated split is paging 14.9 ms (SD model), present 11-12.3 ms (estimate), kernel other ~18 ms (0.62 profile scaled), engine ~48 ms; the last two have +-6 and +-8 ms bars and no 0.71 sample exists (artifacts/quake/h1s-tyr*.txt predate the 0.71 build: worklog-2026-09-21-latepresent.md:84-87). A 1 kHz sampler over a 95 s demo gives ~95,000 samples, +-1% per bucket, which is enough to attribute a 14 ms/frame (15%) term.
routes.evidence: scripts/board/profile-apps.sh:1-40; scripts/board/h1s-report.py:1-30 (--maps/--sym); lvdesk/xshim.c:2777, 9447 (XSHIM_PROF); xlite/xlite.c:1002-1046; docs/worklog-2026-09-21-latepresent.md:84-100 ('74% kernel was scheduling, interrupts and timekeeping - a high WAKEUP rate' at 48 kHz on SDL 1.2); docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md 'Lottery CLOSED' (quiet harness spread 2%).
routes.cheapest_test: This is the cheapest test in the list: three fresh boots, no build, ~25 minutes of board time. It also replaces the present-path estimate (11-12 ms) with a measured number.
routes.effort: Half a day including resolution and a note in docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md.
routes.risks: h1s's 1 kHz sampler phase-locks to the 100 Hz tick (review C09) and biases kernel shares per run - take two captures; PIE bases move per boot so the maps file must be from the same boot; the board is busy now, so this waits.

routes.title: Launch config from the app's own documented switches: -sndspeed 11025 -mem 12 (-zone 32) on the menu Exec lines
routes.steps: Edit buildroot-external/board/esp32-s31/overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf lines 26-28: replace '-mem 20' with '-mem 12 -sndspeed 11025' (timedemo entry) and '-mem 21 -sndspeed 11025' for the Fullscreen/Window play entries (real play adds the 8,552,448-byte edict table: sv_main.c:1355-1356, quakedef.h:74; host hunk print says play needs ~16.9 MB + 3.5 MB cache at 11 kHz). Optionally '-zone 32' (256 kB zone default, 10,640 B used in the host run). Make the Timedemo entry -fullscreen so it measures the same present path as the harness (quake-timedemo.sh:44). Fix the menu comment (the '-mem 13/16 fail' claim is the edict table in play, not the sound cache; and the 8.5 MB is not a sound allocation).
routes.rule_argument: Both switches are TyrQuake's own, documented in man/tyrquake.6 ('-sndspeed n ... Specify sample speed for sound output', '-mem n') and honoured in code (snd_sdl.c:79-81, zone.c:1266-1281). The task text and memory never-force-audio-rate.md say an option the app itself documents counts as supported, and the app then ASKS SDL for 11025 (desired.freq = shm->speed) so nothing is forced behind its back. TENSION to surface: the 2026-09-20 ruling 'steering an app to a cheaper config is still cheating' has no explicit TyrQuake exception on record; the harness and the maps assume it is allowed. The user must ratify before it ships in the menu.
routes.expected_fps: Measured, not estimated: 10.1 fps (-mem 12) / 10.7 fps (-mem 10) vs 8.0 at 48 kHz/-mem 20. For play (server running) use -mem 21; no timedemo number changes.
routes.arithmetic: Sound cache at 11025 = 1,634,944 B vs 7,090,528 B at 48000 (4.34x, pak parse cross-checked by the host 'soundlist' Total bytes resident 1,629,004 vs 7,099,545); shm->buf 16 kB vs 64 kB; mixing 4.35x fewer sample-frames; FIR filter skipped (cutoff_ratio 0.5 early return, snd_mem.c:351) so ~5 s of load-time MAC work disappears from the timed window. Measured effect: 120.9 s -> 90.9-95.6 s (-21 to -25%), majflt 6,601 -> 2,134-2,300, VmSwap 18.3 -> 10.0-12.2 MB, SD read requests 8,480 -> 3,385-4,119. -zone 32: ~55 pages fewer touched, not measurable in fps.
routes.evidence: artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041/run.log; td-sr11k10-061251/run.log; td-tyr071-2-020026/run.log; tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/snd_sdl.c:35,79-81,119,165; common/snd_mem.c:351,455-470; common/zone.c:1266-1281,1291-1320; NQ/sv_main.c:1355-1356; overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf:19-28; scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh:44,71.
routes.cheapest_test: Already done for the timedemo (two fresh boots). For play: launch 'Fullscreen 320x240' with -mem 21 -sndspeed 11025, type 'hunk print' and 'cache print' in the console after 'map e1m1' (both are the app's own console commands) and read REMAINING and the entry count; then an ear check of the sound.
routes.effort: Minutes for the edit; one board session to verify play at -mem 21.
routes.risks: Rule ratification (above). -mem 12 sits at the edge of the timedemo need (8.2 MB hunk + 3.5 MB cache est.); -mem 10 measured slightly faster (10.7) with more I/O, inside the boot-to-boot band. In play, -mem 20 at any rate leaves ~3 MB for the cache and thrashes sounds/models through pak reads + resample on every miss (host e1m1: 32 of 165 cache entries kept at 48 kHz) - hence 21 at 11 kHz.

routes.title: Build stock 0.71's own X11 video/input target (its Linux DEFAULT, not SDL) and give xlite/xshim what it needs: ShmCompletion, XShmGetEventBase, a libXxf86vm client shim
routes.steps: 1) xshim: report a real MIT-SHM event base in the QueryExtension reply (xshim.c:6206-6212 currently 0 with the comment 'we never ShmCompletion') and, in the ShmPutImage handler (xshim.c:5377-5560), when the request's send_event byte is set, queue a 32-byte ShmCompletion event (drawable, minor_event 0, major_event, shmseg, offset) right after the copy - the copy is already synchronous, so the event is correct by construction and needs no completion machinery. 2) xlite: implement XShmGetEventBase (returns that base; not found today - grep of xlite/*.c and xstubs/xstubs.c) next to XShmQueryExtension (xlite_req.c:2731). 3) A libXxf86vm.so client shim in xlite (like xlite/randr) implementing XF86VidModeQueryExtension/QueryVersion/GetModeLine/GetAllModeLines/SwitchToMode/SetViewPort over xshim's existing VidMode server (xshim.c:7980 ff., already used by SDL 1.2's bundled client via the Xext bookkeeping at xlite_req.c:2463-2475). 4) rootfs/build-tyrquake-x11.sh: same make line as build-tyrquake.sh but VID_TARGET=x11 IN_TARGET=x11 SND_TARGET=sdl and X11BASE pointed at staging (Makefile:936-940 adds -lX11 -lXext -lXxf86vm). 5) Run windowed first (no VidMode needed), then -fullscreen.
routes.rule_argument: The X11 target is the stock Makefile's own default for Linux ('VID_TARGET ?= x11 / IN_TARGET ?= x11', Makefile:123-124; USE_SDL is marked 'New (experimental)' at :18): no source edit, no define, no custom library in the app, its data stays on SD. Everything added lives in xlite/xshim (ours). The only judgement call: the user asked for an off-the-shelf binary and this is a different stock build variant of the same source - say so when shipping. Sound stays SDL2 (SND_TARGET=sdl) through 'default' at whatever the app asks.
routes.expected_fps: +3-5% (10.7 -> 11.0-11.2 at 11 kHz). The present path keeps two round trips (ShmCompletion wait + XSync) and the xshim copy stays on the client's critical path, so this is not SDL1-class present.
routes.arithmetic: SDL2 path per frame: app expand into the texture (3.8-5.1 ms) + SDL_BlitCopy texture->SHM segment 153,600 B (3.09 ms quiet, accel-plan.md:35) + XShmPutImage + xshim copy+hash (>=3.09 ms) + XSync wake (~1 ms) = 11-12.3 ms. X11 target per frame (vid_x.c:1038-1054): the renderer draws 8-bit straight into the XShm image at the 16-bit stride and st2_fixup expands IN PLACE right-to-left (vid_x.c:270-285, 76.8 kB read + 153.6 kB write, ~3.8-5.1 ms) + XShmPutImage(send_event True) + wait for ShmCompletion (xshim copy >=3.09 ms + ~1 ms wake) + XSync (~1 ms) = 8-10.2 ms. Saving 3.0-3.5 ms/frame of 93.8 = 3.2-3.7%; x969 = 2.9-3.4 s. Also removes SDL2's per-pump poll() and X11_Pending flush (SDL_x11events.c) and SDL_RenderCopy command-queue overhead (<0.3 ms). Double-buffered XShm (two 153,600 B segments, vid_x.c:80,520-556) adds 153.6 kB of touched memory versus SDL2's texture+segment pair - net zero.
routes.evidence: tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/Makefile:18,105-135,934-940,970-972,1016-1023; common/vid_x.c:71,80,270-285,399-415,455-475,520-556,737-760,832 (XSynchronize, a no-op in xlite: xlite_req.c:1919-1924),963,995-1054; common/in_x11.c:93-105 (warp + null cursor), 333-340 (motion -> IN_CenterMouse), 479-500 (XQueryPointer only before grabbing); lvdesk/xshim.c:5377-5560, 6206-6212, 7980-8000; xlite/xlite_req.c:2463-2475, 2731; xstubs/xstubs.c:163-202; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:162-164 (ShmCompletion: 'our xshim advertises event base 0 because it never sends one').
routes.cheapest_test: Build the binary (container, ~1 min) and run it WINDOWED 320x240 with only steps 1-2 done: it must not hang in 'while (!oktodraw) VID_ProcessEvents()' (vid_x.c:1051) and must turn with the mouse (uinject drag); then one fresh-boot timedemo vs the SDL2 build on the same kernel and -sndspeed/-mem. If the windowed run is not faster than SDL2 windowed by ~3 ms/frame on xsp timers, stop.
routes.effort: 1-2 days: ShmCompletion + event base (hours), libXxf86vm shim (half a day: six requests over an existing server), build script, two board sessions.
routes.risks: vid_x.c's ShmCompletion wait plus XSync make two blocking round trips per frame (~2 ms) - if lvdesk stalls (DIRTYFB) the client waits; keyboard via XLookupKeysym depends on the 2026-09-24 xlite keysym fix; XF86VidMode fullscreen path picks 320x240 from vm_modes (xshim.c:398-405) - verify 'scanout started 640x480' in dmesg, not 800x480; in_x11.c grabs the keyboard (XGrabKeyboard) so a hung game needs the console to kill it; depth: x_visinfo comes from DefaultVisual (vid_x.c:838-845) = xlite's depth-16 root, so st2_fixup runs (16-bit, 153,600 B), not the 32-bit path.

routes.title: Ship the 360 MHz CPU clock (loader + DTS + OpenSBI timebases, vendor clock patch applied per build) after a one-hour soak
routes.steps: 1) bootloader/main/s31_oc.h: S31_CPU_OC_MHZ 0 -> 360 (main.c:400-463 does the esp_pm + XTAL-detour switch). 2) Move the vendor patch from scripts/board/build-oc.sh:38-55 into the Makefile's loader build so /opt/esp-idf (pristine per container run) gets 'case 360: fb_div 9' and the mem 2 / sys 4 / apb 2 dividers on every build ('grep S31_CPU_OC|build-oc|overclock Makefile' finds nothing today). 3) esp32s31.dtsi timebase-frequency and opensbi esp32s31.c S31_TIMEBASE_HZ -> 360000000; make linux AND make opensbi. 4) Flash with scripts/board/flash-trio.sh and run its host/board ratio test (must read ~1.000). 5) The soak the plan names as the ship gate and which has never run: one hour of memtest loops, Doom, desktop and radios (wget throughput, ping loss, BT scan) at 360.
routes.rule_argument: Platform only (loader, OpenSBI, DTS). Radios stay on and are part of the gate. The user's decision is recorded as pending in docs/perf-plan Phase 5 ('Ship decision for 360 - the user's call') because the memory domain runs 180 MHz against a 160 MHz vendor ceiling on the only board.
routes.expected_fps: +3-4% measured on tiopex at 11 kHz (19.2-19.4 -> 20.9/19.2/20.0/19.4, median 19.7); on 0.71 at 11 kHz expect 10.7 -> 11.0-11.1 (estimate: the paging ~15% of wall does not scale with the core).
routes.arithmetic: Clock +12.5%; the 240 MHz mirror arm's slope 0.72 predicted +9% but PSRAM stays on MPLL and 360 delivered +3-4% (median 19.7 vs 19.2-19.4). For 0.71: CPU-bound share ~75-80% of the 93.8 ms frame x (1 - 1/1.035) at the measured tiopex ratio = -2.5 ms -> 91.3 ms = 10.95 fps; if the CPU-bound part scaled with the full 12.5%: -8.3 ms -> 85.5 ms = 11.7 fps (upper bound, not seen on tiopex). Not resolvable on one boot (per-boot band 2-5%); judge on same-hart pingpong (426 us vs ~500 at 320, -15%) plus a 3-boot fps median.
routes.evidence: docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md Phase 5 and log entries '360 MHz WORKS (try 4, #351)', '360 MHz, four boots', '360 MHz radios: no degradation'; bootloader/main/s31_oc.h:9; bootloader/main/main.c:400-463; scripts/board/build-oc.sh:1-30; scripts/board/flash-trio.sh; memory s31-cpu-overclock, overclock-verify-radios.
routes.cheapest_test: The trio already built for the 360 arm exists under images/oc360/ (build-oc.sh output dir); flash-trio.sh + ratio test + one fresh-boot tyr-quake timedemo at -sndspeed 11025 -mem 12: expect ~11 fps; then the one-hour soak before anything ships.
routes.effort: One day for the Makefile hook + timebases + flash, one hour of soak, three fresh boots for the median.
routes.risks: Memory domain 180 MHz vs the vendor ceiling 160 (rtc_clk.c constraints MEM<=160, SYS<=106.67, APB<=53.33): the failure mode is silent PSRAM corruption on the only board; memtest was clean in 3-4 passes but never for an hour under swap. 400 MHz is not on the table until 360 soaks clean (~+5% priced, 25% over spec).

routes.title: Return RAM under the game: udevd off, s31-bt MCL_CURRENT dropped, cold .text..fast trimmed, min_free_kbytes 512, page-cluster 3 tried once
routes.steps: 1) overlay/etc/init.d/S10udevd: stop starting udevd (do not substitute mdev); verify /dev nodes via devtmpfs, USB/BT hotplug and that nothing reads /run/udev (CONFIG_UHID is off anyway). 2) rootfs/s31-bt.c:2121-2139: drop mlockall(MCL_CURRENT), keep the per-buffer mlock of the audio path (:1570-1591); ear-test A2DP afterwards. 3) Re-resolve the 235,520 B .text..fast against the #363+ map with the agg-hot profile and drop whole cold objects from S31_FAST_OBJS (X1-11a); validate on scripts/board/pp-boots.sh (3-boot pingpong medians), because layout moves alone swing pingpong +-15%. 4) sysctl vm.min_free_kbytes 1024 -> 512 (99-s31-memory.conf:17) as a fresh-boot pair on the 11 kHz config (Run D confounded it with swappiness 0). 5) vm.page-cluster 2 -> 3 in physical-slot mode (vma_ra_enabled=0), one fresh-boot pair, judged on SDSTAT fields 1/3 and majflt, not fps.
routes.rule_argument: All platform: init scripts, a daemon of ours, kernel link list, sysctls. Bluetooth stays enabled (s31-bt keeps its audio-path mlocks). Slab is not touched (closed). zram is not proposed (rejected four times).
routes.expected_fps: +2-4% (10.7 -> 11.0-11.1), sign uncertain for min_free and page-cluster; the RAM items are certain as bytes and ~0 to +2% as fps.
routes.arithmetic: Under the 11 kHz game: MemAvailable 432-556 kB, VmRSS 4.7-4.9 MB, VmSwap 10.0-12.2 MB, paging 11.5-14.4 s of 91-96 s. Bytes returned: udevd 160 kB anon + 80 kB /run/udev tmpfs = 240 kB certain (+ ~200 kB of clean cache it stops competing for); s31-bt MCL_CURRENT 100-200 kB (estimate; the 212 kB audit figure predates the MCL_FUTURE removal); cold .text..fast 150-200 kB (estimate: 220,898 B took zero samples pre-DCE, must be re-resolved); min_free_kbytes 512: +744 kB MemAvailable measured idle. Total 0.5-1.4 MB against a ~12 MB touched set with ~4.8 MB resident. No fault-vs-resident model exists here (the 09-21 -mem table shows faults non-monotonic in heap), so: -10-25% of paging = -1.2-3.6 s of 91 s = +1.3-4%. page-cluster 3: the -mem 20 run averaged 11.4 KiB per read (cluster 2 merging ~3 slots); 8 slots per request costs 2.49 + 0.67 = 3.16 ms vs ~2.73 for 11 KiB, so it pays only above ~75% hit rate on the extra slots; review put a 30-40% regression chance on it; potential -3 to -5 s if hits hold. Together these cannot remove the 11.5-14.4 s paging term; at best they halve it (-6 s = +6.5%).
routes.evidence: docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:178 (C51 udevd), :157-159 and :245 (T2.3, cluster), :319 (C50 min_free), :213-216 and :287 (X1-11a); docs/current-state.md:4915-4920, 6541-6556, 3942; rootfs/s31-bt.c:1570-1591, 2121-2139; overlay/etc/sysctl.d/99-s31-memory.conf:17,93-99; overlay/etc/init.d/S10udevd:31-63; images/System.map __text_fast_start c083ac10 / __text_fast_end c0874410; Makefile:1278 (libasound is ALREADY in xip2 - the 'move libasound to XIP' lever in two maps is stale).
routes.cheapest_test: Two sysctls need no build: PRE='sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=512' scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh mf512 -mem 12 -sndspeed 11025 with QUAKE_BIN=./tyr-quake, and the same with vm.page-cluster=3; fresh boot each, compare SDSTAT reads/sectors and majflt to td-sr11k12-060041. udevd: rename S10udevd on the card, one boot, plug a USB mouse, then the same timedemo.
routes.effort: Half a day for the sysctl pairs; a day for udevd/s31-bt with hotplug and ear checks; a day for the .text..fast re-resolution with pp-boots validation.
routes.risks: min_free 512 can move reclaim into the fault path under a swapping game (the reason it was raised to 1024 was streaming-read throughput); page-cluster 3 evicts a resident page for every speculative one at 436 kB free; udevd removal changes hotplug semantics (memory s31-usb-hotplug-after-8bitdo is still OPEN); trimming .text..fast has already produced a 5% regression once when chosen by share instead of frequency (profile-apps.sh header).

routes.title: C86 libc math in the Buildroot musl (integer floor family, single-precision float trig, s31fp mul/add ahead of libgcc) - and the s31fp preload for tyr-quake only if the user rules it platform
routes.steps: 1) Arch override files in the crosstool musl (configs/riscv32-esp-linux-musl.config, musl 1.2.5): floor/ceil/trunc/round/modf by integer bit manipulation (bit-exact); sinf/cosf/atan2f in single precision with fmadd.s and a 3-part Cody-Waite reduction (<=1 ulp); link rootfs/s31fp's __muldf3/__adddf3/conv into libc.so ahead of libgcc. 2) Rebuild the toolchain + rootfs (make toolchain-source then the rootfs), gate on the desktop canary and Tyrian. 3) Separately, if ratified: LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libs31fp.so on the tyr-quake Exec line (all 9 signatures match rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg byte-for-byte; S31FP=0 disables).
routes.rule_argument: libc.so is a Buildroot-built shared library the app loads dynamically - platform by every rule statement and the review's 'legal part' (perf-review:96-104). The preload half is the open rule question: the task text calls C86/s31fp platform; the review (C87, perf-review:367) and memory s31-soft-double-cost call patching the app's own libgcc copies the redline route. It is listed here as within_rules for the libc part only; do not enable the preload for tyr-quake without the user's word.
routes.expected_fps: +1-2% (10.7 -> 10.8-10.9). Ceiling 4.17% of CPU0 if all libc math were free.
routes.arithmetic: 0.71's double footprint equals 0.62's (call-site census: __extendsfdf2 199/182, __truncdfsf2 154/144, __muldf3 111/107, __adddf3 83/70, __subdf3 70/70; the per-edge 'double fu, newzi' lives in both r_edge.c:421,680 vs 0.62 :410; D_DrawSpans8 has no soft-double site in either). On the only Quake profile (tiopex, 12,000 samples): __adddf3 201 + __muldf3 94 + __subdf3 60 + __truncdfsf2 25 = 380 = 3.17% of CPU0, libm bodies 0.91%. s31fp alone: (261 x (1-1/1.4)) + (94 x (1-1/2.5)) = 75 + 56 = 131 samples = 1.1% of CPU0 -> fps 1/(0.86/1.011 + 0.14) - 1 = +0.9%. Full C86: +1.2-3.5% of CPU0 (two lenses) -> +0.2-0.6 fps on a 16.6 fps boot, i.e. +1-2% here; parts not additive.
routes.evidence: docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:96-104, 367; rootfs/s31fp/preload.c:1-30, sigs.h; docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:525-541 (mul 738 -> 296 ns, add/sub 423 -> 308 ns; 'Left built, verified, NOT enabled'); images/libc.nm (__sindf, __cosdf, __rem_pio2f, floor, sin); tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/r_edge.c:421,680; common/mathlib.c:317-324 (AngleVectors double sin/cos); llvm-objdump census of rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg vs rootfs/tiopex-quake.dbg.
routes.cheapest_test: The preload is a zero-build A/B/A on one boot (LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libs31fp.so S31FP_DEBUG=1 on the timedemo line; it prints what it patched) and bounds the whole libgcc family at ~1%; if the A-to-A gap swallows it, the libc work is not worth days for Quake alone (it still helps Tyrian's FM synth).
routes.effort: Days for the libc overrides and toolchain rebuild; minutes for the preload test.
routes.risks: Float trig <=1 ulp, not bit-identical (flag); a toolchain rebuild changes every library's codegen; the preload skips objects dlopen()ed later (SDL2's X11 backend is dlopen'd, but xlite's own double use is unmeasured and minor); rule question on the preload.

routes.title: Rejected or rule-violating routes, priced so they are not re-proposed: viewsize 100 / cvars, capped ALSA device, SDL2 library fast paths, MIT-SHM adoption, XIP app, zram, swappiness 0, page-cluster in VMA mode
routes.steps: None to apply. Listed with their numbers: (a) '+set viewsize 100' (or any cvar: snd_filterquality, loadas8bit, _snd_mixahead, vid_vsync 0, d_mipcap, -surfcachesize, -particles) - app config steering; viewsize 100 would drop the 3D view from 216 to 192 rows (12.5% fewer rasterised pixels, ~ -3.5 ms/frame, +4%) and is exactly the 0.62-vs-0.71 default difference. (b) s31route max_rate / AUDIODEV steering - the audio hard rule; and it buys nothing over -sndspeed (both end at shm->speed 11025). (c) SDL2 SW_LockTexture aliasing the window surface to delete the 3.09 ms blit - patches a stock library (review C89/X3-11 'violates-rules'; the task lists Buildroot SDL2 as platform, so this is 'arguable, not settled' and needs a ruling; technically it also re-opens the read-while-drawing race of adoption). (d) MIT-SHM segment adoption in xshim: 31.7 fps adopted but flickers, illegal by the protocol contract (xshim.c:5422-5450, dead-end #15). (e) tyr-quake in XIP flash: rule (memory no-apps-in-flash) and fps-neutral anyway (10.7 vs 10.9). (f) zram: rejected four times (s31-swap.conf); (g) swappiness 0: OOM-kills Quake with 62 MB of swap free; (h) 32-bit SDL2 visual: 10.7 -> 5.5 on chocolate-doom (#81); (i) PPA/GDMA for the ShmPutImage copy: the SysV segment is outside lcd_reserved (xshim.c:194-197). (j) libSDL2 -O2 or Zcb/Zcmp toolchain rebuild: <=+0.5% until a profile shows SDL2 above 5% of the frame, and the toolchain -march change would silently change the stock app's codegen (toolchain-wrapper.c:390-401).
routes.rule_argument: (a) and (b): the user's rulings of 2026-09-20 ('steering an app to a cheaper config is still cheating') and 2026-09-23 (never force a rate); (c): patching stock SDL is recorded violates-rules and is unresolved as 'platform library' - flagged for the user, not recommended; (d)-(i): recorded rejections with numbers; (j): rule risk plus no evidence.
routes.expected_fps: (a) +4% est. (viewsize), 0 at 11 kHz for the sound cvars; (b) 0 over -sndspeed; (c) +3.3% est. (3.09 ms of 93.8); (d) +11% but illegal; (e)-(i) 0 or negative.
routes.arithmetic: viewsize: rows 240 - sb_lines; 0.71 default 110 -> sb_lines 24 -> 216 rows; 0.62/id default 100 -> sb_lines 48 -> 192 rows; rasteriser cost ~30 ms/frame x 24/216 = 3.3 ms. SDL2 blit: 153,600 B at 3.09 ms quiet = 3.3% of 93.8 ms. Adoption: 31.7 vs 29.4 fps (+7.8%) on Doom, flickering.
routes.evidence: tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/screen.c:200 vs sdlquake-master/source/screen.c:115; memory s31-never-rebuild-client-apps, never-force-audio-rate, no-apps-in-flash; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:369, 374, 391, 400, 409, 470; lvdesk/xshim.c:194-197, 5422-5450; overlay/etc/s31-swap.conf; docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:287-293; docs/worklog-2026-09-21-latepresent.md:113-129.
