routes.title: Attribute the missing ~30 ms/frame BEFORE building anything: one PC profile of stock 0.71 at its own 11025 Hz, plus three runtime-knob bounds
routes.steps: (1) Board free: run scripts/board/profile-apps.sh with APPS="tyrq:cd /root/quake && DISPLAY=:0 HOME=/root/quake AUDIODEV=default ./tyr-quake id1 -basedir /root/quake -sndspeed 11025 -mem 12 -width 320 -height 240 -fullscreen -condebug +timedemo demo1" and the pre-sample sleep raised from 12 s to 25 s (0.71 reaches the demo ~10 s later than tiopex; artifacts/quake/h1s-062518/run.sh used 25). Two 4 s captures, /proc/PID/maps saved during the capture. Resolve with `scripts/board/h1s-report.py images/System.map <pcs> 60 --maps maps.txt --symdir images` (images/tq.nm is rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg's table, main at 0xa340 matches the ELF; sdl2.nm and libc.nm exist). (2) Three fresh-boot timedemos, same args, one knob each: XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT=1 in the client's environment (present-family ceiling), XSHIM_NOROWDMG=1 in lvdesk's environment (row-hash cost), and -window instead of -fullscreen (present-path comparison). (3) Widen the harness first for anything under ~9 fps: quake-timedemo.sh:71 runs runsh 240/170 and killed the first 8 fps run at 237 s. (4) Decide: if user code R_*/D_*/CL_* is >=60% of CPU0 with idle <10%, the gap is the 0.71 engine and no rules-compliant route reaches 20 - say so; if idle/fault/reclaim/memcpy/XSync-wait classes are >=30%, R3-R5 can be sized honestly; if SDL2 (SDL_BlitCopy, SDL_Blit*, X11_*) is >=15%, R3 (X11 backend) is the route.
routes.rule_argument: Measurement only: the hart0 PC sampler needs nothing in the target (profile-apps.sh:5-9), the two env knobs already exist in our code (xlite/xlite.c:1002-1046, lvdesk/xshim.c:614-624) and -window is a documented switch (man/tyrquake.6, vid_mode.c:1221). Nothing is shipped from this route; XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT is a bound, never a default (it tears).
routes.expected_fps: No gain by itself. It decides whether 20 fps is reachable at all: today every known platform lever compounds to ~+16% (R2-R8 below: 10.7 x 1.04 x 1.035 x 1.03 x 1.02 x 1.02 x 1.01 = ~12.4 fps), so 20 fps needs ~35-40 ms/frame that nobody has located, and only a profile can say whether it is platform-side.
routes.arithmetic: Measured: stock 0.71 at -sndspeed 11025 = 969 frames in 95.6 s (-mem 12, 10.1 fps) / 90.9 s (-mem 10, 10.7 fps) = 94-99 ms/frame; tiopex 0.62+SDL1 on the same kernel at 11 kHz = 45-46 ms/frame (21.3/21.6 fps). Gap 48-53 ms. Accounted from code (estimates): SDL2 present path ~9 ms more than SDL1 (expand 76,800 px x 49-66 ns = 3.8-5.1 ms + SDL_BlitCopy 153,600 B = 3.09 ms quiet + xshim copy+hash >=3.09 ms + ~1 ms wake, vs ~2.5 ms); faults +4 ms/frame (2,134-2,300 x 2.7 ms / 969 vs 887 x 2.7 / 969); 0.71's per-frame savesurfs/saveedges memcpy ~2-3 ms (r_main.c:1212-1215, up to ~250 kB at 102 MB/s); 0.71 renders viewsize 110 (screen.c:200) vs 0.62's 100 (sdlquake-master/source/screen.c:115) = +11% pixels ~ +3-4 ms. Sum 18-20 ms. ~30 ms/frame unexplained. Target 20 fps = 50 ms/frame.
routes.evidence: artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041/run.log (RESULT 969 frames 95.6 s 10.1 fps; QUAKE majflt=2134 VmRSS 4748 kB VmSwap 12172 kB; MemAvailable 556 kB); td-sr11k10-061251/run.log (90.9 s, 10.7 fps, majflt 2300, VmSwap 10024); td-sr22k14-060630/run.log (119.6 s, 8.1 fps, majflt 4440); td-tyr071-2-020026/run.log (8.0 fps, majflt 6601, VmSwap 18340); td-sr11k12-060041/panel.png (640x480 centred with 80 px bars = the 320x240 mode PPA-scaled, and 'Sound Initialized: 16 bits @ 11025Hz'); docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md log 'C39 SHIPS' (21.3/21.6); h1s-report.py on artifacts/quake/h1s-062518/pcs.txt with --fit tiopex-quake=images/tiopex-quake.nm (94.9% coverage): user 50.9%, kernel flash 28.4%, RAM text 11.8%, libs 7.8%, idle 8.6%; tyrquake-0.71/common/vid_sdl.c:440-483; docs/accel-plan.md:31-35; scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh:71; scripts/board/profile-apps.sh:1-60, h1s-report.py usage lines 1-40; images/tq.nm (1,488 symbols, main 0xa340). Note: the rules map's claim that the 11025/-mem 12 arm is void is stale - td--mem-054943 died on the 256 MB default heap, the later td-sr11k12/td-sr22k14/td-sr11k10 arms ran.
routes.cheapest_test: ~10 min of board time per piece: profile-apps.sh with the tyrq APPS line (one boot, two 4 s captures), then three quake-timedemo.sh boots with PRE/env knobs. Read the h1s split first (user program vs SDL2 vs libc vs kernel classes vs idle); the three knob arms only bound the present family.
routes.effort: 2-3 hours of board time in <=10 min pieces; no build.
routes.risks: The 1 kHz sampler is phase-locked to the 100 Hz tick (perf-review C09) so kernel shares are biased per run; the sampler CTRL/BUF addresses move with every loader build (profile-apps.sh:26-27, check with nm on hello_world.elf); h1s cannot see which fault or wait is which - idle lumps XSync waits, fault I/O and audio sleeps together, so a large idle share needs the SDSTAT/majflt line to split it; XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT tears and must never be left in an Exec line.

routes.title: App options only: -sndspeed 11025 -mem 12 (timedemo) / sized -mem for play, on the launcher Exec line - the app's own documented switches, and nothing from its cvar/config channel
routes.steps: (1) menu.conf Quake block (overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf:26-28): replace '-mem 20' with '-sndspeed 11025 -mem 12' on the Timedemo entry and make it -fullscreen like the harness (quake-timedemo.sh:44) so measured and played paths match; for the Play entries (a server runs: 8192-edict table 8,552,448 B on rv32 + progs + world) use '-sndspeed 11025 -mem 21' per the memory map's arithmetic (play hunk ~16.9 MB + 3.5 MB cache set), accepting that play is swap-backed; optionally '-zone 32' (documented, ~224 kB less memset). (2) Do NOT use -sndspeed 22050 (8.1 fps measured: the 64-tap S_FilterSfx pad + the plug resampler, because the I2S mask has no 22050) and do NOT use a capped ALSA device. (3) Everything else the app offers is either inert here or config steering: -sndbits 8 (plugin offers S16 only, snd_sdl.c:136-160), loadas8bit (all 120 shareware sounds already 8-bit), vid_vsync (SW renderer claims PRESENTVSYNC, no wait), and performance cvars (viewsize 100, r_lerpmodels 0, d_mipcap, snd_filterquality 0, -surfcachesize, -particles) which the user's 2026-09-20 'still cheating' ruling forbids - listed so they are not re-proposed.
routes.rule_argument: The task's own rule text says an option the app itself documents counts as supported: '-sndspeed n' is in man/tyrquake.6 ('Specify sample speed for sound output') and honoured at snd_sdl.c:78-81; '-mem n'/'-heapsize n' at zone.c:1266-1281; the rate is chosen by the app at the source (desired.freq), not behind its back by a capped device. Residual ambiguity: the 2026-09-20 ruling calls steering an app to a cheaper config 'still cheating' and there is no explicit user ruling for TyrQuake - the audio clause carves out documented switches, the config clause does not; flag it, do not assume it.
routes.expected_fps: Measured, not estimated: 8.0 (48 kHz, -mem 20) -> 10.1 (-mem 12) / 10.7 (-mem 10) fps, i.e. +26-34%; the -mem 12 vs 10 difference is inside the 2-10% per-boot band. This is the base every other route multiplies; it does not reach 20.
routes.arithmetic: Sound cache for demo1's precache: 7,090,528 B at 48 kHz -> 1,634,944 B at 11025 (4.34x, all 120 shareware WAVs are 11025 Hz 8-bit so ResampleSfx is a 1:1 copy and the FIR is skipped, snd_mem.c:351,464); shm->buffer 64 kB -> 16 kB; mixer work 48000/11025 = 4.35x fewer sample-frames (bounded at 1-3% of the core anyway). Paging term: 6,601 faults x ~2.7 ms = 17.8 s of 120.9 s (15%) -> 2,134 x 2.7 = 5.8 s of 95.6 s (6%). Frame time 120.9/969 = 125 ms -> 95.6/969 = 99 ms.
routes.evidence: tyrquake-0.71/common/snd_sdl.c:35 (SND_DEFAULT_RATE 48000), :78-81 (-sndspeed), :165 (shm->speed = obtained.freq), :171-174 (shm->samples); common/zone.c:1266-1281; common/snd_mem.c:455-470 (cache size scales with shm->speed); artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041, td-sr11k10-061251, td-sr22k14-060630, td-tyr071-2-020026 run.log RESULT/QUAKE lines; td-sr11k12-060041/panel.png ('16 bits @ 11025Hz'); linux-71-port/sound/soc/espressif/esp32s31-i2s.c:520-523 (rate mask, no 22050); overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf:23-28; scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh:44; NQ/sv_main.c:1355-1356 + quakedef.h:74 (MAX_EDICTS 8192) for the play -mem; memory note s31-never-rebuild-client-apps ('steering an app to a cheaper config is still cheating').
routes.cheapest_test: Already measured (three artifacts). One more fresh boot at -mem 12 gives the spread; for play, one board 'hunk print' after 'map e1m1' at -mem 21 replaces the ~16.9 MB rv32 estimate.
routes.effort: Minutes (one menu.conf edit) once the user rules on -sndspeed.
routes.risks: User may classify -sndspeed as config steering (then the honest number stays 8.0 fps at 48 kHz and every route below starts from there); -mem 10/12 will thrash the sound/model cache in real play (host e1m1 run at -mem 20/11k kept 141 of 165 entries; below that every miss is an SD read + resample on the mixer path, snd_mix.c:199); -mem 21 in play is ~20 MB touched on a 15 MB board, so play fps will sit below the timedemo's.

routes.title: Stock 0.71 on its own X11 backend (VID_TARGET=x11 IN_TARGET=x11 SND_TARGET=sdl) - the Makefile's default Linux drivers - with xshim sending the ShmCompletion event that client consumes
routes.steps: (1) xshim: allocate a real MIT-SHM event base in the QueryExtension reply (xshim.c:6206-6212 answers 0 and never sends one) and after the ShmPutImage copy emit XShmCompletionEvent (drawable, major/minor opcode, shmseg, offset) when send_event=True - protocol-required, ~40 lines. (2) Buildroot: enable BR2_PACKAGE_XLIB_LIBXXF86VM (stock X.org library + xf86vidmodeproto headers) in buildroot-external/configs/esp32s31_rootfs_defconfig; ship libXxf86vm.so.1 in the overlay/XIP list. (3) rootfs/build-tyrquake-x11.sh: same make invocation as build-tyrquake.sh but without USE_SDL=Y and with VID_TARGET=x11 IN_TARGET=x11 SND_TARGET=sdl (X11BASE=<staging>); output rootfs/tyr-quake-x11, deployed to /root/quake. (4) Validate on the host first: build the same configuration natively and run demo1 under Xvfb -depth 16 with a real X server (memory note s31-xvfb-ground-truth) - checks st2_fixup's 16-bit in-place expansion and the completion wait. (5) One fresh-boot timedemo; then mouse-look by hand/uinject.
routes.rule_argument: Unmodified source, its own Makefile, its own driver variables: VID_TARGET/IN_TARGET/SND_TARGET are the variables USE_SDL=Y sets (Makefile:105-110) and x11 is the Makefile's own default for Linux (Makefile:119-120, 'All other unix can default to X11'); USE_SDL is documented as 'New (experimental) SDL ... targets' (Makefile:18). The -DX11 define is added by the Makefile itself (Makefile:935), not by us. libXxf86vm is a stock Buildroot package; ShmCompletion is server-side X protocol; sound still goes through SDL2 -> ALSA -> s31route at the app's own -sndspeed. Argue this to the user explicitly rather than assume it: it is a different build configuration of the same stock app.
routes.expected_fps: ESTIMATE +3-5% on the timedemo (10.7 -> 11.0-11.2) plus a mouse-look path with no per-event round trip; and it is the cleanest discriminator for R1: if it lands at ~11 fps the 2x is the 0.71 engine, if it lands near 20 the 2x was SDL2. Not a route to 20 on its own by the arithmetic below.
routes.arithmetic: Client-side bytes per 320x240 frame: SDL2 path = 76.8 kB read + 153.6 kB written (VID_Update expand, vid_sdl.c:469-476) + 153.6 kB read + 153.6 kB written (SDL_BlitCopy texture->SHM surface, SDL_render_sw.c COPY -> SDL_BlitSurface) + xshim's 153.6 kB copy before the reply = ~845 kB; vid_x.c path = st2_fixup in place in the SHM image (vid_x.c:401-411) + xshim copy = ~384 kB. Saves the 153,600 B SDL_BlitCopy = 3.09 ms quiet / 11.98 ms loaded (accel-plan.md:35, CPU column) = 3-5% of a 94-99 ms frame. Costs one extra round trip per rect (the completion wait, vid_x.c:1050-1052, then XSync :1059), ~1 ms cross-hart. Mouse: in_x11 recentres with XSelectInput + XWarpPointer + XSelectInput and no XSync (in_x11.c:89-96), against SDL2's XWarpPointer + XSync per motion event (SDL_x11mouse.c:351,357).
routes.evidence: tyrquake-0.71/Makefile:18,105-125,934-946,966-975,1023-1027; common/vid_x.c:399-411 (depth switch), :832 (XSynchronize - a no-op in xlite, xlite_req.c:1919-1924), :1035-1060 (XShmPutImage send_event True, oktodraw wait, XSync), :964 (oktodraw on the completion event); common/in_x11.c:89-96, :333-342, :471-484; lvdesk/xshim.c:6206-6212 (MIT-SHM event base 0, 'we never ShmCompletion'), :5422-5450 (copy always); xlite/xlite_req.c:2461-2470 (Xext bookkeeping already serves SDL1's bundled Xxf86vm, which is X.org's code); Buildroot staging has libX11.so/XShm.h but no libXxf86vm or xf86vmode.h (docker ls); docs/accel-plan.md:31-35; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:162-168 (T2.4: ShmCompletion was rejected only because SDL 1.2/2 never consume it - vid_x.c does).
routes.cheapest_test: Host: build the x11 configuration natively and run 'timedemo demo1' under Xvfb -depth 16 (no board). Board: one fresh-boot quake-timedemo.sh with QUAKE_BIN=./tyr-quake-x11 after the xshim change is deployed (deploy.py over Wi-Fi), ~5 min.
routes.effort: 0.5-1 day: xshim event base + send, one Buildroot package, a build script, host validation, one board boot.
routes.risks: vid_x.c hangs without ShmCompletion (the while(!oktodraw) loop); xlite's Display/Xext internals were exercised by SDL1's bundled Xxf86vm, not by a standalone libXxf86vm.so.1 - same source, unverified binding; xlite may lack an Xlib entry the x11 backend uses (x11_core.c/vid_x11_common.c: XkbSetDetectableAutoRepeat, XF86VidModeSetViewPort, XLookupString paths) - the host Xvfb run does not test xlite, only the app; vid_x.c does an XQueryPointer round trip per frame until the grab completes (in_x11.c:471-484); in fullscreen it uses the VidMode path (same as prboom) not RandR; the user may still regard a non-SDL build configuration as 'steering' - ask.

routes.title: Ship the 360 MHz CPU clock (loader s31_oc.h, vendor clock patch applied by the Makefile, DTS + OpenSBI timebases, soak)
routes.steps: (1) bootloader/main/s31_oc.h S31_CPU_OC_MHZ 0 -> 360 (main.c:400-463 does the esp_pm + XTAL-detour switch). (2) Make the Makefile apply the vendor patch on every loader build (clk_tree_ll.h 'case 360: fb_div 9', rtc_clk.c dividers mem 2/sys 4/apb 2) - today only scripts/board/build-oc.sh:38-55 does it and the container IDF is pristine per run. (3) esp32s31.dtsi timebase-frequency and opensbi S31_TIMEBASE_HZ to 360000000: make linux AND make opensbi. (4) Flash with scripts/board/flash-trio.sh and its host/board ratio test (must read ~1.000; make flash-* would overwrite the trio via sync-images). (5) The gate the plan names and nobody has run: one hour at 360 of memtest loops, Doom, the desktop, radios (Wi-Fi throughput/loss, BT scan), then two quiet Quake boots. (6) Post-ship regression pass (Doom 44.5 median, sdl1 canary 8.55 ms, xcalc, OpenTyrian).
routes.rule_argument: Platform only (loader, OpenSBI, DTS); no app, library or config change; Bluetooth and Wi-Fi stay on and were measured inside their band at 360. The plan records it as 'the user's call' because the memory domain runs 180 MHz on a 160 MHz vendor ceiling on the only board.
routes.expected_fps: +3-4%, measured on tiopex at 11 kHz (19.2-19.4 -> median 19.7, two of four boots >= 20). On stock 0.71 at 10.7 fps: ~11.0-11.2 (estimate: the app's own code is a larger share of 0.71's frame, so if anything slightly more). Not a route to 20 alone; 400 MHz is priced at ~+5%, not +18%.
routes.arithmetic: Clock +12.5%; the 240 MHz mirror arm gave slope 0.72 (15.4/16.3 vs 19.2-19.4 for -25%), which predicted +9%, but the measured 360 result was +3-4% because PSRAM stays on MPLL and the frame is more memory-bound than the both-clocks arm showed. fps = 1/(0.86/1.035 + 0.14) - 1 = +3% on a main thread 86% busy.
routes.evidence: docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md Phase 2 ('DONE - STEEP', slope ~0.72), Phase 5 ('360 MHz arm IN FLIGHT', '360 arm: RADIOS OK', 'Ship decision for 360 - the user's call': Quake 20.9/19.2/20.0/19.4, memtest 2 MB x 3-4 clean on both CPUs, gate 22/22, wget 615/538 vs 628/701 KB/s); bootloader/main/s31_oc.h:9; bootloader/main/main.c:400-463; scripts/board/build-oc.sh:38-55; scripts/board/flash-trio.sh; memory notes s31-cpu-overclock, overclock-verify-radios; grep of Makefile for S31_CPU_OC/build-oc/overclock: not found.
routes.cheapest_test: The trio already exists in images/oc360: flash-trio.sh + ratio test + one quiet 0.71 timedemo at -sndspeed 11025 -mem 12 (~10 min) says what 360 buys this binary; the hour-long soak is the ship gate, not the test.
routes.effort: ~1 day including the Makefile hook and the soak.
routes.risks: MEM domain 12.5% over the vendor ceiling permanently on the only board (silent PSRAM corruption is the failure mode; memtest clean so far, never soaked for an hour); Wi-Fi throughput read ~10% lower on n=2 (inside the band, to be re-read in the soak); a mismatched trio (loader vs DTS vs OpenSBI) gives a false result (#346 was discarded for exactly that).

routes.title: Return RAM to the 0.71 working set: libasound into XIP, udevd off, s31-bt MCL_CURRENT dropped, page-cluster 3 in physical-slot mode - judged on majflt and SDSTAT, not fps
routes.steps: (1) XIP census first (scripts/board/xip-census.sh) with tyr-quake running: which pages the audio thread and present path fault from SD (libasound 943,548 B is deliberately on SD for lvdesk's sake, Makefile:927-931, but SDL2's ALSA thread touches it every 46 ms period at 11025 Hz). (2) Make room: ~780 kB free across the two XIP images (perf-plan Phase 3c) is less than libasound; evict something the census shows idle (libSDL2_mixer 600 kB if no menu app maps it, or libpng/libz/xcalc), then add usr/lib/libasound.so.2.0.0 to XIP_ROOTS, make xip images + sync-images + flash both rootfs images. (3) C51: stop starting udevd (overlay/etc/init.d/S10udevd) after verifying USB/BT hotplug and that nothing reads /run/udev; +~240 kB anon+tmpfs. (4) s31-bt: drop mlockall(MCL_CURRENT), keep the per-buffer mlock of the audio path (rootfs/s31-bt.c:1570-1591, 2121-2139); verify A2DP by ear afterwards. (5) vm.page-cluster 2 -> 3 with vma_ra_enabled=0, one fresh boot, judged on /sys/block/mmcblk0/stat fields 1 and 3 and majflt.
routes.rule_argument: Platform placement and kernel knobs only: libasound is a Buildroot shared library the app loads dynamically (flash is for platform code; the app and its data stay on SD), udevd/s31-bt are our daemons, sysctls are boot-time config. Bluetooth stays enabled (only a lock scope changes). Slab is not touched.
routes.expected_fps: ESTIMATE +2-3% (10.7 -> ~11.0); hard ceiling +6.4% if every major fault vanished. The recorded verdicts (dead-end #80 libSDL into XIP 16.2 -> 16.0; C51 '~0 fps') were priced on tiopex's 887-1,352 faults; 0.71 takes 2,134-2,300 at 11 kHz, still only ~6% of wall, so the ceiling is small.
routes.arithmetic: Paging term at 11025/-mem 12: 2,134 faults x ~2.7 ms (2.49 ms + 11.4 KiB/48 MB/s, the measured average request in the -mem 20 run) = 5.8 s of 95.6 s = 6.1%; at -mem 10: 2,300 x 2.7 = 6.2 s of 90.9 = 6.8%. If the four items cut faults by a third (libasound/udevd/s31-bt free ~1.4 MB against a 4.7 MB RSS at 432-556 kB MemAvailable): ~2%. page-cluster 3: 8 slots per request cost 2.49 + 32 KiB/48 MB/s = 3.16 ms vs ~2.73 ms for the 11.4 KiB average; breaks even only above ~75% hit rate on the extra slots.
routes.evidence: Makefile:919-931 (XIP_ROOTS and the libasound comment); docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md Phase 3c (~780 kB free, XIP census entry); docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:178 (C51), :157-159 (T2.3), :469 (dead-end #80); rootfs/s31-bt.c:1570-1591, 2121-2139; overlay/etc/init.d/S10udevd:31-63; overlay/etc/sysctl.d/99-s31-memory.conf:93-99; artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041/run.log (MEM MemAvailable 556 kB; SDSTAT 4653 reads/155526 sectors vs td--mem-054943's fresh-boot baseline); docs/current-state.md:2036-2044 (SD request model 2.49 ms + size/48 MB/s).
routes.cheapest_test: One fresh-boot quake-timedemo.sh per change (~4 min each), reading QUAKE majflt and SDSTAT fields 1/3; fps only as the multi-boot median at the end. The libasound move needs a flash of both rootfs images (make xip + sync-images + flash-xip-rootfs, ~2 min).
routes.effort: 1-2 days including the census, the XIP eviction decision and the udevd hotplug check.
routes.risks: Evicting a library from XIP to the SD lower layer exposed a stale card copy once (memory s31-xip-is-for-things-that-run) - checksum the card copy first; udevd removal changes hotplug semantics (CONFIG_UHID is off anyway); page-cluster 3 has a recorded 30-40% chance of regressing at ~500 kB MemAvailable; every item is below the 2-10% per-boot band on fps, so judge on the fault counters only.

routes.title: Preload rootfs/s31fp/libs31fp.so on the tyr-quake Exec line (LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libs31fp.so) - the app's statically linked soft-double helpers patched at load time
routes.steps: (1) Confirm the rule: the task text calls s31fp 'considered platform', the review's C87 (perf-review:367) calls patching the app's own libgcc copies 'the redline route' and reserves C86 for libc-side work; the memory note says 'Built, verified, NOT enabled'. Get the user's yes before shipping. (2) menu.conf: prefix the tyr-quake Exec lines with LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libs31fp.so (S31FP=0 disables, S31FP_DEBUG=1 lists what was patched); ship libs31fp.so in XIP. (3) Verify by S31FP_DEBUG=1 that all six routines patched (signatures matched byte-for-byte against rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg: __muldf3 0x745c2, __adddf3 0x7359e, __subdf3 0x74b16, __floatsidf 0x7546c, __fixdfsi 0x7532a, __floatunsidf 0x754bc). (4) Same-boot A/B/A timedemo or bundle with R4/R5; it is below the per-boot band alone.
routes.rule_argument: By the task's own text ('C86 = an LD_PRELOAD soft-double replacement ... is considered platform') and the Exec line being platform. The binary on disk is untouched (private COW page, preload.c:15-19), nothing is rebuilt or relinked. The contrary record (C87 redline, review:367; memory s31-soft-double-cost) is real, so this is marked within-rules conditionally on the user's confirmation.
routes.expected_fps: ESTIMATE +~2% (10.7 -> ~10.9). The app-local soft-double share on the only Quake profile (tiopex, same double footprint as 0.71 by the call-site census) is __muldf3 2.6% + __extendsfdf2 0.45% + __fixdfsi 0.28% of CPU0; s31fp speeds mul 2.5x and the conversions, leaves __extendsfdf2/__divdf3/compares alone.
routes.arithmetic: Savings = 308 x (1 - 1/2.5) + 34 x 0.5 = 185 + 17 = 202 of 12,000 samples = 1.7% of CPU0; fps = 1/(0.86/1.017 + 0.14) - 1 = +1.5%. The per-span double in D_DrawZSpans (d_scan.c:889 'double zi', 4.6% of samples as a function) is where most of the app's __muldf3 calls come from; the libc-side block (__adddf3 201 + __muldf3 94 + __subdf3 60 + __truncdfsf2 25 = 3.17%) is R8's, not this route's.
routes.evidence: rootfs/s31fp/preload.c:1-27 (mechanism), :47-54 (six routines), sigs.h; docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:525-541 (mul 738 -> 296 ns, add/sub 423 -> 308 ns, 'Left built, verified, NOT enabled'); h1s-report.py --fit on artifacts/quake/h1s-062518/pcs.txt: tiopex-quake:__muldf3 308 samples (2.6%), __extendsfdf2 54, __fixdfsi 34, D_DrawZSpans 554 (4.6%); tyrquake-0.71/common/d_scan.c:885-935; docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:96-104 (T1.7), :367 (C87); cpu-levers map: 9/9 signatures match rootfs/tyr-quake.dbg today.
routes.cheapest_test: S31FP_DEBUG=1 launch (patched count) then one same-boot A/B/A timedemo with the A-to-A gap as the error bar; bit-exactness is already established over 4M operand pairs.
routes.effort: One Exec-line edit plus the rule confirmation; an hour to verify.
routes.risks: Rule: two records contradict the task text; preload.c does not scan objects dlopen()ed after the constructor (SDL2 dlopens xlite/libXi/libXrandr at runtime - minor, their double use is unmeasured); libSDL2 itself links libSDL2 directly so it is scanned; gain is below the per-boot band, so never judge it on a single fps number.

routes.title: Playability, not fps: XInput2 raw motion in xshim (+ GenericEvent/cookie plumbing in xlite) so SDL2 stops warping-and-syncing the pointer on every motion event during mouse-look
routes.steps: (1) Measure first: with tyr-quake in a timedemo and 'uinject drag' running, count WarpPointer (core opcode 41) and GetInputFocus per second with xshim's per-op counters (XSHIM_PROF), and compare the timedemo's fps with and without injected motion in one boot (A/B/A). (2) xshim: answer XQueryExtension('XInputExtension') with a major opcode, implement XIQueryVersion (answer 2.0 so SDL skips multitouch), XISelectEvents (RawMotion/RawButtonPress/RawButtonRelease masks on the root), XIGetClientPointer, XIWarpPointer, XIQueryDevice/XIFreeDeviceInfo stubs, and emit XI_RawMotion as GenericEvent (type 35) with the FP3232 valuator layout per pointer motion for clients that selected it. (3) xlite: GenericEvent decode + XGetEventData/XFreeEventData with the XESetWireToEventCookie hook the real libXi.so.6 (already in the Buildroot target: usr/lib/libXi.so.6.1.0, dlopened by SDL2 via SDL_config.h:400) registers - or provide the cookie fill directly. (4) Verify with sdl2keys + uinject that relative deltas arrive and no warps are issued in relative mode. Skip this route entirely if R3 ships (in_x11 warps without a sync).
routes.rule_argument: xlite, xshim and libXi (a stock Buildroot library) are platform; SDL2 and the app are untouched - SDL2 already prefers XI2 when the server offers it (SDL_x11mouse.c:381-384 returns SDL_Unsupported only because X11_Xinput2IsInitialized() is false; SDL_mouse.c:1145-1153 then falls back to warp mode).
routes.expected_fps: 0% on the timedemo (no pointer motion). During continuous mouse-look: ESTIMATE the client currently spends 15-19% of its wall in warp round trips (125 Hz mouse x ~1.2-1.5 ms XWarpPointer+XSync each) plus lvdesk's warp handling and the synthetic MotionNotify per warp (xshim.c:7241-7297); removing it is the difference between '20 fps in the timedemo' and '20 fps while turning'.
routes.arithmetic: Per motion event in warp mode: SDL_PrivateSendMouseMotion -> X11_WarpMouse -> WarpMouseInternal = XWarpPointer + X11_XSync (SDL_x11mouse.c:351,357) = one request + one GetInputFocus round trip; cross-hart round trip ~1.0 ms (plan Phase 3: pingpong cross-hart 1,035-1,044 us) + xshim/lvdesk warp processing. A full-speed USB mouse reports at 125 Hz -> 125 x 1.2-1.5 ms = 150-190 ms per second of motion = 15-19% of the client's wall; at 10 fps that is 1.5-1.9 round trips per frame. Unmeasured; the xsp counters give the real event rate (motion compression may fold some).
routes.evidence: Buildroot sdl2-2.32.10 src/video/x11/SDL_x11mouse.c:319-358 (WarpMouseInternal), :381-384; src/events/SDL_mouse.c:558-576 (warp per motion when relative_mode_warp), :1142-1153 (fallback); src/video/x11/SDL_x11xinput2.c:113-143 (needs XQueryExtension('XInputExtension') + XIQueryVersion >= 2.0); src/video/x11/SDL_x11sym.h XINPUT2 module (9 symbols); SDL_config.h:400,406; lvdesk/xshim.c:6165-6212 (extension list: no XInputExtension), :7241-7297 (WarpPointer + synthetic MotionNotify); xlite has no GenericEvent/XGetEventData (grep: none); docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md 2026-09-24 entry ('trace: motion + recentring warps + cursor hide'); Buildroot target usr/lib/libXi.so.6.1.0 present.
routes.cheapest_test: One boot: timedemo with and without 'uinject drag' (same boot, A/B/A) plus XSHIM_PROF counts of opcode 41 and GetInputFocus per second - 10 minutes, no build; it says what the warp storm costs before anything is written.
routes.effort: 2-3 days (XI2 wire format, cookie plumbing, SDL2's exact mask selection to read from SDL_x11xinput2.c first).
routes.risks: XI2 changes SDL2's keyboard/touch selection too (version 2.2 enables multitouch; answer 2.0); SDL2's XI2 code path uses XIGetClientPointer/XIWarpPointer for the enter/leave-relative warps; the hidden cursor and grab semantics must still hold (VT-capture invariant); the whole route is moot if R3 (in_x11 backend) is taken.

routes.title: Small platform bundle, only after R1's bounds say the family is worth it: C86 libc math (floor family bit-exact, single-precision float trig, s31fp mul/add linked into libc.so) + xshim/lvdesk present-path trims for a fullscreen 16-bit ShmPutImage
routes.steps: (1) C86: musl arch overrides in the crosstool libc (images/libc.nm shows __sindf/__cosdf/__rem_pio2f and libc's own __adddf3/__muldf3/__divdf3) - floor/ceil/trunc/round/modf by integer bit manipulation, sinf/cosf/atan2f in single precision with fmadd.s, s31fp's muldf3/adddf3/conv linked ahead of libgcc; gate on the LD_PRELOAD caller census (which libm entry points tyr-quake imports: atan atan2 atanf atof cosf exp floor ldexp logf pow sin sinf tan). (2) xshim: skip the FNV row hash when the target is a fullscreen 16-bit window (or stand it down adaptively as lvdesk's fsrh_probe does, lvdesk.c:4700-4730) - measure with XSHIM_NOROWDMG=1 first. (3) xshim/lvdesk: let the ShmPutImage copy land in kms_fs_map directly in fullscreen so fs_present's second 153,600 B memcpy (lvdesk.c:4862-4865) disappears - CPU1 headroom only. (4) Bundle and judge on pingpong/xsp per-op timings; fps as a multi-boot median at the end.
routes.rule_argument: libc.so is a Buildroot/crosstool-built shared library the app loads dynamically - the review's 'legal part' (C86); xshim/lvdesk are ours. No SDL2 patch (C89/X3-11 verdicts: patching stock SDL is violates-rules by the history lens even though the task lists SDL2 as fair game - needs a user ruling, and the only SDL2-side item worth anything, handing SW_LockTexture the window surface, is <=3.09 ms = 3%).
routes.expected_fps: ESTIMATE +1.5-4% combined (10.7 -> 10.9-11.1): C86 +1.2-3.5% of CPU0 (review's two lenses, not additive with R6), hash skip <=0.6 ms/frame (<1%), the kms_fs_map write ~0-1% (post-reply work on a 63.7%-idle CPU1 is 0% on client fps by construction).
routes.arithmetic: C86: libc-side soft double on the tiopex profile = 380/12,000 = 3.17% of CPU0 (+ libm bodies 0.91%), s31fp does not speed __adddf3/__subdf3 (67% of that block) so the mechanism lens gives 2.5-3.5% and the physics lens 1.2-2.0%. Hash: 38,400 word iterations x ~3-5 cycles at 320 MHz = 0.36-0.6 ms per frame on the client's critical path (xshim.c:5480-5560, replies leave before late_present_drain at :9633-9638). NOSYNCWAIT bounds this whole family: pre-reply copy 3.09 ms + hash + ~1 ms wake = 4-5 ms = 4-5% of a 94-99 ms frame - the ceiling for any legal lever here.
routes.evidence: docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:96-104 (T1.7/C86), :219-221 (post-reply work is 0% on client fps), :369 (C89), :374 (X3-11); images/libc.nm; lvdesk/xshim.c:614-624, 5452-5560, 9633-9638; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:4700-4730, 4840-4885; docs/accel-plan.md:31-35; docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md Phase 1 XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT entry (closed at <=2.5% on the SDL1 canary - SDL2's pre-reply work is 153,600 B, so it must be re-bounded on this client, which R1 does); Phase 4 'C86 gated on the LD_PRELOAD caller census'.
routes.cheapest_test: R1's XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT and XSHIM_NOROWDMG boots bound the present half for free; for C86, an LD_PRELOAD caller census (which libm symbols tyr-quake calls and how often) on one boot before any libc work.
routes.effort: C86: days (arch override files, toolchain rebuild, <=1 ulp trig to flag); present trims: half a day.
routes.risks: Everything here is below the per-boot band and must be bundled; C86's float trig is not bit-identical (flag to the user); a libc rebuild changes every process's libc (regression pass required: Doom 44.5, canary 8.55 ms, xcalc, OpenTyrian); writing ShmPutImage straight into the dumb buffer could make the pre-reply copy slower if the mapping is not cached (dead-end #10 says the aliased-uncached path is 7.6 MB/s).

result.reasoning:
R1 is a measurement-only route (no fps claimed, nothing shipped), so the "unmeasured assumption" default does not bite: its expected_fps is "no gain". Checked against the repo:

RULES - OK. The hart0 PC sampler needs nothing in the target (scripts/board/profile-apps.sh:6-9; bootloader/main/s31_vcpu.c:963-974, ctrl word 1..4000 samples = the 4 s captures). -sndspeed and -window are documented switches (tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/man/tyrquake.6:111 and :57; common/snd_sdl.c:78-81 reads -sndspeed), which the task's rule explicitly counts as supported. XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT exists (xlite/xlite.c ~1002-1030, getenv at ~1017) and XSHIM_NOROWDMG exists with the stated semantics (lvdesk/xshim.c:614-624, rowdmg_on = getenv==NULL). Neither is proposed as a default.

NUMBERS - correct. artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041/run.log: RESULT 969 frames 95.6 s 10.1 fps, majflt 2134, VmRSS 4748, VmSwap 12172, MemAvailable 556; td-sr11k10-061251: 90.9 s 10.7 fps, majflt 2300, VmSwap 10024; td-sr22k14-060630: 119.6 s 8.1 fps majflt 4440; td-tyr071-2-020026: 8.0 fps majflt 6601 VmSwap 18340. 95.6/969 = 98.7 ms, 90.9/969 = 93.8 ms; tiopex 21.3/21.6 fps = 46.9/46.3 ms; gap 47-52 ms (route says 48-53, immaterial). Compounding 1.04x1.035x1.03x1.02x1.02x1.01 = 1.165, x10.7 = 12.5 (route 12.4) - arithmetic fine, but the R2-R8 multipliers themselves are not verifiable from this route. viewsize 110 vs 100 confirmed (tyrquake-0.71/common/screen.c:200 vs sdlquake-master/source/screen.c:115); savesurfs/saveedges memcpy confirmed at r_main.c:1211-1214. The "in flight" note is right: the 11k/-mem 12, 11k/-mem 10 and 22k/-mem 14 arms completed 06:00-06:12 today; td--mem-054943 was the one that died.

ALREADY MEASURED? Partly, for one sub-step only. No PC profile of stock 0.71 exists: artifacts/quake/h1s-tyr.txt / h1s-tyr2.txt (Sep 21, 4000 samples each) predate the 0.71 arms, have no maps, and are not referenced anywhere in docs; the perf-review's Quake profile is tiopex (perf-review:21, h1s-062518 fitted to tiopex-quake.dbg). So step (1) is genuinely new and is the decisive one. Step (2a) XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT was already bounded and CLOSED on the sdl1 canary (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:98 and :694, artifacts/perf-plan/nosyncwait-114744: -5% inside an 11% A-to-A gap, family ceiling <=2.5% Quake) - that was an SDL1 client; for the SDL2 present path it is unmeasured, so the arm is justified only if the profile shows a wait class, and should be dropped otherwise. Steps (2b) and (2c) are unmeasured on 0.71 (every 0.71 arm so far is -fullscreen: td-tyr071-*/td-sr* run.sh).

TWO DEFECTS IN STEP (1) AS WRITTEN (repairable, not refuting): (a) profile-apps.sh's maps capture matches ps with /[t]yrquake/ (line ~53), which does not match the binary name "tyr-quake" - maps.txt would be empty and no user PC resolves; the pattern needs [t]yr-quake (quake-timedemo.sh already uses that). (b) h1s-report.py --symdir looks up <mapped basename>.nm (h1s-report.py:175-178), i.e. images/tyr-quake.nm and images/libSDL2-2.0.so.0.nm, neither of which exists; images/tq.nm and sdl2.nm must be passed as --sym tyr-quake=images/tq.nm --sym libSDL2-2.0.so.0=images/sdl2.nm. --fit cannot rescue it: tq.nm is a 3-column nm (no sizes) and --fit requires nm -S (usage line 32). Without both fixes the route's user-vs-SDL2-vs-libc split - the whole point - comes back as an unresolved program bucket. Also C09 (perf-review:377) is correctly cited: kernel shares from a single 4 s capture are aliased against the tick, so two captures is the minimum, and the idle bucket needs the SDSTAT/majflt line to split faults from XSync waits from audio sleeps, as the route says.

DOUBLE-COUNTING: none - it claims no gain. Verdict: survives, with the two tooling fixes made a precondition and step (2a) made conditional on the profile.
result.corrected_expected_fps: No change: 10.1-10.7 fps (measured, -sndspeed 11025, -mem 12/-mem 10). Measurement-only; the ~12.4-12.5 fps compounded figure it quotes for R2-R8 is arithmetically consistent but rests on those routes' unverified multipliers, not on R1.

result.reasoning:
NUMBERS CHECK OUT, MECHANISM AND RULE DO NOT.

1. Measured values verified against the artifacts (all single fresh-boot runs through scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh, which reboots per arm): artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041/run.log "RESULT 969 frames 95.6 seconds 10.1 fps", majflt=2134, VmSwap 12172 kB, panel.png shows "Sound Initialized: 16 bits @ 11025Hz"; td-sr11k10-061251: 10.7 fps, majflt=2300; td-sr22k14-060630: 8.1 fps, majflt=4440; td-tyr071-2-020026 (48 kHz, -mem 20): 8.0 fps, majflt=6601, VmSwap 18340 kB. The second 48 kHz run (td-tyr071-1-015209) and the -mem10 48 kHz run (td-tyr071-mem10-225310) were both killed by the runsh watchdog (RS_TIMEKILL) and carry no result, so the 8.0 baseline is n=1 and every arm is n=1. The per-boot lottery is recorded as 10-17% (docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:22) with a 2% quiet-harness spread (:786); +26% is above the band but no arm has a spread.

2. RULE: refuted on the strict reading. The audio this route produces is bit-identical to the capped s31route_11k device the user rejected BY EAR on 2026-09-23. Proof: SDL2 2.32.10 src/audio/SDL_audio.c:1587-1589 - legacy SDL_OpenAudio with a non-NULL obtained passes SDL_AUDIO_ALLOW_ANY_CHANGE, so with the capped device TyrQuake asked 48000, was granted 11025 and set shm->speed = obtained.freq = 11025 (snd_sdl.c:165); with -sndspeed 11025 it asks 11025 and gets 11025 - same shm->speed, same cache size (snd_mem.c:455-470), same 1:1 ResampleSfx branch (snd_mem.c:75-78), same skipped FIR (snd_mem.c:351), same route-plugin path (rootfs/s31route.c:531-538 says it in so many words: "Offered only 11025, it is granted 11025 and nothing in the game changes"). The recorded verdict on that output: "Quake at the capped 11025 Hz device does not [sound fine]" (perf-plan:302-303), "sounded wrong by ear" (overlay asound.conf:12-13), "the sound was wrong by ear" (quake-timedemo.sh:22-25). Doom at 11025 through the same codec row sounded fine (perf-plan:303), so the wrongness is Quake-at-11025 itself, which -sndspeed reproduces exactly. The route also switches off the app's own quality feature: at 11025 the 64-tap windowed-sinc upsampler (snd_filterquality default 3, snd_mem.c:178,192-204) is bypassed by construction (cutoff_ratio >= 0.5, snd_mem.c:351). The task's rate clause admits a documented switch (man/tyrquake.6:111-112 even says "Default 11025", contradicting snd_sdl.c:35's 48000), but the separate 2026-09-20 ruling that steering an app to a cheaper config is "still cheating" (memory s31-never-rebuild-client-apps) has no TyrQuake exception, there is no user ruling on -sndspeed anywhere in docs/ (grep: not found), and the route itself lists this as the first risk. A switch chosen solely to make the app do less work, whose output the user already judged wrong, is config steering for performance.

3. ARITHMETIC: the cache sizes 7,090,528 / 1,634,944 B and the play-hunk 8,552,448 / 16.9 MB are not found anywhere in the repo (grep docs, artifacts, tyrquake): unsourced. The 4.34 ratio is just 48000/11025 = 4.354 (correct in form; pak0.pak is not in the repo, so "all 120 WAVs are 11025 8-bit" is unverifiable here). 2.7 ms/fault is not a recorded number; docs/current-state.md:7794-7796 says 2.5-4 ms and the SD model (2.49 ms + 16 KiB/48 MB/s = 2.83 ms for a page-cluster=2 read) agrees, so it is a fair estimate. But the route's own mechanism does not add up: 4,467 fewer faults x 2.7 ms = 12.1 s, mixer "1-3%" <= 3.6 s, against 25.3 s actually saved - ~10 s of the gain is unexplained by the stated mechanism. The fps is measured so this does not change the number, but the paging story is incomplete.

4. The GOAL is a playable Quake; the measured 10.1 fps is a -mem 12 timedemo. The route's Play entries use -mem 21 (an rv32 estimate that needs a board 'hunk print' the route itself defers), ~20 MB touched on a 15.3 MB board, and the route concedes play fps sits below the timedemo's. So the playable configuration's fps is unmeasured, and even the timedemo number (10.1, 10.7) is half the 20 fps target.

5. Not previously rejected as such (perf-review C84/C85 and row 24 concern the 22050 mask and the capped device, not -sndspeed), and no double-count - it is a base, not a multiplier. Minor: menu.conf is at buildroot-external/board/esp32-s31/overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf:26-28 (lines match); MAX_EDICTS at NQ/quakedef.h:74 and sv_main.c:1355-1356 check; -zone at zone.c:1316-1320 and man:35-37 check; loadas8bit auto-set only below 8 MB (snd_dma.c:252) so inert at -mem 12 as claimed.

Verdict: refuted. The fps is measured but rests on an unruled rule question, and the sound it ships was already rejected by ear.
result.corrected_expected_fps: If the user rules -sndspeed 11025 permitted: 10.1 fps timedemo at -mem 12 (10.7 at -mem 10), each n=1 fresh boot, per-boot band 10-17%; the Play configuration (-mem 21, swap-backed) is unmeasured and by the route's own account lower. If not permitted (strict reading, and the same audio was rejected by ear on 09-23): 8.0 fps at 48 kHz/-mem 20, n=1. Neither reaches 20.

10.1 fps at -sndspeed 11025 -mem 12 (artifacts/quake/td-sr11k12-060041: 969 frames / 95.6 s, majflt 2,134, VmSwap 12.2 MB) and 10.7 at -mem 10 (td-sr11k10-061251: 90.9 s, majflt 2,300, VmSwap 10.0 MB), each a single fresh-boot run (quake-timedemo.sh resets before every run, line 70). Baseline 8.0 at 48 kHz -mem 20 (td-tyr071-2-020026, n=1). Treat as 10-11 fps timedemo, +26-34% over 8.0, until 5 repeats give a spread; the 12-vs-10 gap is inside the plan's stated +-10% per-boot band. Play entry (-sndspeed 11025 -mem 21, server + 8192 edicts) is not measured; labelled estimate: it puts roughly today's -mem 20 swap footprint back, so play sits near 8 fps, not 10. Nothing here approaches 20; it is a base other levers multiply, and any route that also books the sound-cache shrink double-counts.
result.reasoning:
RULE. The task's own audio clause says a documented command-line switch counts as explicit support. -sndspeed is documented in tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/man/tyrquake.6:111-112 ("Specify sample speed for sound output. Default 11025." - the app's own manual calls 11025 the default) and honoured at common/snd_sdl.c:79-81; -mem/-heapsize at common/zone.c:1266-1281, man page :31-34; -zone at :35-37. The pristine tarball (tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71.tar.gz, diff -rq clean apart from bin/ and build/) has SND_DEFAULT_RATE 48000 at snd_sdl.c:35, so the 48/11025 inconsistency is upstream's, not ours. The chain is unforced end to end: s31route offers 8000-48000 (rootfs/s31route.c:545-546, asound.conf has no capped device), 11025 is in ESP32S31_I2S_RATES (linux-71-port/sound/soc/espressif/esp32s31-i2s.c:520-523) and the ES8389 has a 64x row for it since 2026-09-19 (memory s31-es8389-no-mclk-ratio, patches/0042). The launcher Exec line is listed as fair game in the task. Residual: the 2026-09-20 'cheaper config is still cheating' ruling was about OpenTyrian and app rebuilds (memory s31-never-rebuild-client-apps); the task text carves documented switches out for the rate clause only. -mem is not a quality trade (the app defaults to a 256 MB heap, zone.c:1279, and every shipped Exec line already carries -mem 20, menu.conf:26-28). The route flags this correctly; the user must still say yes. 22050 is rightly excluded: absent from the I2S mask, so plug's linear converter runs, and it measured 8.1 (td-sr22k14-060630).

ARITHMETIC. The fps figures are measured, not estimated; all four artifacts exist with RESULT lines and their run.sh shows exactly the claimed arguments. Paging term checks: 2.49 ms + 16 KB (page-cluster 2) / 48 MB/s = 2.83 ms per cluster -> 6,601 x 2.83 = 18.7 s of 120.9 (15%), 2,134 x 2.83 = 6.0 s of 95.6 (6%), matching the route within rounding. Sound-cache scaling (snd_mem.c:455-470, stepscale = info->rate / shm->speed) is correct. (b) Saving verified but smaller than claimed: SDL2's path is SW_LockTexture (direct pixels) -> vid_sdl.c:469-476 expand -> SDL_RenderCopy -> Blit_to_Screen -> SDL_BlitSurface (build/sdl2-2.32.10/src/render/software/SDL_render_sw.c:307) -> SW_RenderPresent -> SDL_UpdateWindowSurface (:964-971) -> XShmPutImage + ONE XSync (src/video/x11/SDL_x11framebuffer.c:183, :219). vid_x.c's st2_fixup is in place (vid_x.c:269-285; xshim root depth is 16, xshim.c:2612-2630, so depth 16 and st2_fixup apply - the task's '32 bpp' is not what xshim advertises). (c) Cost understated: vid_x.c:1050-1052 waits `while (!oktodraw) VID_ProcessEvents()`; VID_ProcessEvents (vid_x.c:931-938) spins on XPending, which in xlite is XEventsQueued(QueuedAfterFlush) = a NON-BLOCKING socket read per call (xlite/xlite.c:1081, :1063-1072) for the whole duration of xshim's copy, and THEN XSync at vid_x.c:1059 - two round trips per frame where SDL2 has one. (a) xlite's XShmPutImage discards send_event and hardcodes r[30]=0 (xlite/xlite_req.c:2832,2856): the xshim-only change in step (1) never receives send_event=True; xlite must change too (unlisted). (b) XShmGetEventBase, which vid_x.c needs for x_shmeventtype, is defined neither in xlite (no hit in xlite/*.c) nor in the board's stub libXext (xstubs/xstubs.c:163-195 exports only XShmQueryExtension/QueryVersion/CreateImage/Attach); the real libXext.so.6.4.0 is on X11_REPLACEMENTS (Makefile:996-997) and deleted from the target (post-build.sh:98-105). REFUTATION 2 - the completion wait hangs under xlite even after (1). vid_x.c:1050-1052 spins while(!oktodraw) VID_ProcessEvents(); VID_ProcessEvents (vid_x.c:931-940) loops on XPending; xlite's XPending -> XEventsQueued with an empty queue does a non-blocking poll+recvmsg and NEVER flushes the output buffer (xlite.c:1051-1081, xlite_read_more 498-506), while xlite's XShmPutImage deliberately does not flush (xlite_req.c:2860-2880, 'DO NOT FLUSH HERE'). The put never reaches xshim; the loop is infinite. Once a flush is added, the loop is still a ~0.15 ms poll() syscall spin on CPU0 for the ~3 ms of xshim's copy, where the SDL2 path sleeps in a single blocking read that the sound thread can use.

REFUTATION 3 - arithmetic omits the cost side it names. Per frame, vid_x.c does put -> flush -> wait for the event (read) -> XSync (write + read) = one extra write+read versus SDL2's put+GetInputFocus in one write and one read (xlite_req.c:2866-2872). Recorded af_unix cost is write 2.1 ms / read 1.3 ms (memory s31-socket-syscalls-cost-ms, XSHIM_PROF), i.e. ~3.4 ms extra, or at most 2.3 ms if the T2.4 ceiling (2.5% of the frame, perf-review T2.4) is taken. The saving is one 153.6 kB same-format blit ~3.09 ms (accel-plan.md:35 quiet; the 11.98 ms 'loaded' figure is a desktop-with-continuous-pointer-motion number and does not apply to a fullscreen timedemo). Net: -0.3 to +0.8 ms on a 93.5 ms frame, -0.3% to +0.9% - not +3-5%. The '~1 ms cross-hart round trip' is an unmeasured assumption contradicted by the recorded numbers, which triggers the default refuted=true.

REFUTATION 4 - double count. The ShmCompletion/last-round-trip half is the T2.4 family (perf-review-2026-09-23.md T2.4: ceiling +2.5% Quake) that the plan closed after XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT measured -5% inside an 11% A-to-A gap (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md Phase 1). WHY REFUTED - the expected fps rests on an unmeasured transfer, and the measured number it borrows is overstated:
(1) Every 360 MHz Quake number (20.9/19.2/20.0/19.4, perf-plan:554-560, 570-576) was taken on tiopex-quake (TyrQuake 0.62 + SDL 1.2 8bpp glue, no mouse) at the capped s31route_11k device - a configuration the HARD RULE at perf-plan:300-310 retroactively declares a forced-rate number, and a binary the task marks a dead end. Nothing at 360 has ever been run on rootfs/tyr-quake (stock 0.71, SDL2). The route's own "cheapest_test" concedes this.
(2) The borrowed gain is +3-4% only on the mean (19.875/19.3). By median - the plan's own rule - 19.7 vs 19.2-19.4 is +1.5-2.6%, and two of the four 360 boots (19.2, 19.4) are exactly the 320 baseline, i.e. half the boots showed zero gain, with a 9% spread against 320's 2% (perf-plan:570-576 says two more boots were owed before the number is quoted; the plan's log never records them).
(3) The direction-of-transfer argument is backward. The route says 0.71 should gain "if anything slightly more" because more of its frame is app code. The measured 360 shortfall (+3% vs the +9% the 0.72 mirror slope predicted) was attributed by the plan to PSRAM staying on MPLL - memory-bound work does not scale with the CPU PLL (perf-plan:554-560, memory s31-cpu-overclock). What 0.71 adds over tiopex is exactly that kind of work: SDL2's 32 bpp software renderer moving ~300 kB/frame (4x tiopex's 76 kB) through PSRAM, plus swap. Stock 0.71 is swap-backed at every measured setting: artifacts/quake/td-sr11k10-061251 (-sndspeed 11025, -mem 10): 10.7 fps, majflt 2,300, VmSwap 10,024 kB; td-sr11k12-060041: 10.1 fps, 2,134 majflt, 12.2 MB swap; td-sr22k14-060630: 8.1 fps, 4,440 majflt; td-slim11k10-063205: 12.4 fps, 1,595 majflt. Swap faults are SD-bound (2.49 ms + size/48 MB/s, 2 ms floor) and do not scale with the clock: at page-cluster 2, 2,300 faults x ~2.8 ms is an estimated ~6.5 s of the 90.9 s run (~7%) that 360 cannot touch. So 0.71's clock-scalable share is smaller than tiopex's, not larger; the +3-4% is an upper bound, not a floor.
(4) The arithmetic shown is circular: fps = 1/(0.86/1.035 + 0.14) plugs the measured +3.5% back in as the speed-up k and reads out +3%. The clock ratio actually available is 1.125; with the review's 86%/14% model (docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:200) that gives 1/(0.86/1.125 + 0.14) = +10.6%, which is what was NOT observed - the model, built for tiopex, does not describe this frame. The "86% busy" figure has no measurement for 0.71.
(5) Double-counting: the review's combined landing figure (perf-review:200, "at the safer 360 MHz point, 18.2-18.7") already includes this lever, so any route that cites 17.5-18.2 -> 18.2-18.7 and also adds R4 counts it twice; and R4 is mutually exclusive with, not additive to, any 400 MHz route.
(6) Risk and gate: the memory domain at 180 MHz on a 160 ceiling is permanent on the only board, the hour-long soak the route lists as its ship gate has never run (memtest only 2 MB x 3-4 per check), Wi-Fi throughput read ~10% lower on n=2 (perf-plan:245-249), and the memory rule board-test-10-minute-rule forbids a single hour-long result - the soak has to be sliced into <=10 min results. flash-trio.sh's ratio test is correct and necessary (scripts/board/flash-trio.sh:26), and a mismatched trio did produce a discarded arm (#346, perf-plan:227-235).

Net: R4 is in-rules but its +3-4% on 0.71 is an unmeasured assumption stacked on a generous reading of a rule-violating tiopex measurement; even at face value it is +0.2-0.4 fps toward a 20 fps target that sits at 10.7-12.4 today.

REFUTED ON THE EXPECTED FPS - it rests on three unmeasured or disowned inputs:
(1) The evidence base is a forced-rate number. The only 360 measurements (plan log 2026-09-23: 20.9/19.2/20.0/19.4 vs 19.2-19.4 at 320) were tiopex-quake on the s31route_11k capped device. The HARD RULE entry (plan lines 301-306) states that every Quake fps taken on that device 'including today's 19.5-21.6 is a forced-rate number'. R4 quotes those numbers as its gain.
(2) The measured gain is inside the noise floor. Median 19.7/19.3 = +2.1%, mean 19.875/19.3 = +3.0%; the 360 four-boot spread is 9% (19.2-20.9), one boot equals the 320 baseline, the 320 baseline is n=2 with a 1% spread. SD of the four = 0.78, SE = 0.39, delta 0.58: t ~ 1.5. The plan's own rule ('nothing below the lottery ships on its own fps number'; CLAUDE.md 'establish the noise floor before believing a result') applies. The corroborating instrument disagrees with itself: pingpong moved 500 -> 426 us at 360 (slope ~1.2) but only 500 -> 525-529 at 240 (slope ~0.2), so at least one of those is a per-boot artefact.
(3) The transfer to stock 0.71 is assumed and in the wrong direction. The '10.7 fps' base is not found in docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md, docs/current-state.md or any artifact; the recorded honest number is 8.0 fps at 48 kHz/-mem 20 swap-backed (6,601 majflt, VmSwap 18.3 MB; plan line 294). The stock 0.71 PC-sample profiles (artifacts/perf-plan/tq-profile-061910/raw.txt and tq-profile2-064453/raw.txt, 4,000 samples each, maps.txt puts tyr-quake text at 0x690d1000-0x6916d000) attribute 40.7% / 47.1% of samples to the kernel, 29.3% / 30.6% to the app text, 13.5-18.7% to libraries. That is MORE kernel/I-O-bound than tiopex (review: 'Quake's frame is 59% its own code'), not less, so 'the app's own code is a larger share of 0.71's frame, so if anything slightly more' is unmeasured and points the wrong way. At 48 kHz the SD wait alone is 6,601 majflt x (2.49 ms + 16 KiB/48 MB/s = 2.82 ms) = 18.6 s of the 121 s demo = ~15% of wall time that a CPU clock cannot touch at all (the SD and PSRAM/MPLL are on other clocks). The -sndspeed 11025/-mem 12 arm that would change this is in flight, not recorded.
(4) Arithmetic error: fps = 1/(0.86/1.035 + 0.14) - 1 feeds an already whole-frame measured +3.5% through the review's 86%-busy/14%-wait model (review line 200, a tiopex model) a second time - the waits are discounted twice. The correct reading of the tiopex data is simply +2-3% whole-frame.
(5) Double-count warning: the review's and plan's combined landing figure '18.2-18.7 at 360 MHz' (plan line 17, review line 200) already contains this lever; any route that quotes that band AND adds R4 counts 360 twice.
Risk not refuted but restated: MEM domain permanently at 180 MHz on a 160 MHz vendor ceiling on the only board, memtest 2 MB x 3-4 (minutes) is the entire integrity evidence, the hour soak has never run, and the task forbids touching the board so it cannot run now. Wi-Fi throughput read ~10% lower on n=2.

Transferred to the recorded stock 0.71 number (8.0 fps at 48 kHz/-mem 20, ~15% of wall in SD waits that do not scale, 41-47% of samples in the kernel): 8.0 -> ~8.15-8.25 fps (8.0 x (1 + 0.025 x 0.85)), i.e. +0.2 fps, an estimate. (1) RULE. The user's 2026-09-20 redline (memory s31-never-rebuild-client-apps) reads 'never rebuild, relink, RECONFIGURE or wrap a client application ... to make it faster' and 'steering an app to a cheaper config is still cheating'; experiments off the installed path need the user's say-so first. The route's only motive is performance/diagnosis: the mouse already works on the SDL2 build (docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:290-293). Picking VID_TARGET=x11 over USE_SDL=Y is a deliberate reconfiguration of the app's build for speed, so strictly it fails the rule even though x11 is the Makefile's Linux default (tyrquake-0.71/Makefile:119-121). The proposal itself says 'ask'. Contested at best; not within_rules as claimed.

(2) AS WRITTEN IT HANGS. Step (1) changes xshim only, but xlite's XShmPutImage discards the send_event argument and hardcodes the wire byte: xlite/xlite_req.c:2832 '(void)send_event' and :2856 'r[30] = 0; /* sendEvent: no completion */'. vid_x.c's True (common/vid_x.c:1039-1043) never reaches xshim, no ShmCompletion is ever sent, and 'while (!oktodraw) VID_ProcessEvents();' (vid_x.c:1050-1052) spins forever on the first frame. docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:164 (T2.4) already recorded 'our xlite hardcodes sendEvent=0'. Fixable in xlite, but the route missed it and its cheapest test (host Xvfb) cannot see it. XShmGetEventBase (vid_x.c) is also absent from xlite's XLITE_IMPL set (symbol diff of x11_core.c/vid_x11_common.c/vid_x.c/in_x11.c vs xlite/): it must come from the staging libXext.so.6.4.0 - unverified which libXext the board ships (xlite_req.c:2465 says libXext's Xext entries 'were stubs').

(3) ARITHMETIC AGAINST THE RECORD. The 10.7 fps baseline is not stock 0.71's number: perf-review:233/:455 '10.7 vs 10.9' is tiopex-quake XIP-vs-SD and :413 '10.7 -> 15.1' is tiopex 22 kHz -> 11 kHz. Stock 0.71 at its own 48 kHz is 8.0 fps, 6,601 majflt, 18 MB VmSwap, -mem 20 (perf-plan:290-295), i.e. a 125 ms frame whose recorded residue is 'anonymous heap swap' (perf-review:233), which the x11 backend does not touch (same Hunk, same sndspeed; two SHM framebuffers, vid_x.c ResetSharedFrameBuffers, vs SDL2's texture+surface - a wash on RSS). The saved SDL_BlitCopy (SDL_render_sw.c:307 SDL_BlitSurface; SDL_x11framebuffer.c:183/219 XShmPutImage+XSync) is one 153,600 B copy = 3.09 ms quiet (accel-plan.md:35, ppabench row-by-row memcpy on an idle board) = 2.5% of a 125 ms frame at best. The cost side is under-priced: the proposal's '~1 ms cross-hart' is unsourced, while the record says af_unix write 2.1 ms, read 1.3 ms, poll 0.15 ms (memory s31-socket-syscalls-cost-ms, XSHIM_PROF). SDL2's frame is ONE write (xlite deliberately does not flush between ShmPutImage and XSync so both leave in one write, xlite_req.c:2862-2870) plus one reply read = ~3.4 ms. vid_x.c's frame is ShmPutImage, then XPending = XEventsQueued(QueuedAfterFlush) (xlite/xlite.c:1081, a flush/write plus a drain per spin iteration) until the completion arrives, then XSync = GetInputFocus write + reply read (xlite.c:1018-1040): >= 2 writes + 2 reads = ~6.8 ms, plus xshim's own event write. Extra ~3.4 ms/frame cancels the ~3.1 ms saved. Net ~0 within noise; the +3-5% rests on the unsourced 1 ms.

(4) ALREADY BOUNDED/CLOSED. T2.4 (perf-review:162-168) caps the whole 'last X round trip' family at +2.5% absolute (ppoll share 1.8%), and the maximal control XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT measured -5% inside an 11% A-to-A gap and was CLOSED (perf-plan Phase 1). This route adds a second wait per frame to that family. The R1-discriminator claim double-counts: the 8.0 vs ~14-20 gap is recorded as the 48 kHz swap-backed sound cache, so an x11 build lands near 8 and discriminates nothing about SDL2.

Not a route to 20 fps; the proposal concedes as much.

1. Wrong number for the per-warp cost. The route prices one XWarpPointer+XSync at "cross-hart pingpong 1,035-1,044 us" (perf-plan Phase 3). That figure is (a) a futex wake ping-pong between two pinned threads, not an X round trip (rootfs/pingpong.c:1-13, :38, :43), and (b) the number from kernel #343 = C20, marked "NOT SHIPPED" (docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:121-126); the shipped cross-hart figure is 825-851 (perf-plan:562). The measured X round trip is different and larger: XSync 6.4 -> 5.4-6.1 ms over af_unix (docs/x11-review.md:29-36, 2026-08-31; read 1.3 ms + write 2.1 ms, x11-review.md:178-181; current-state.md:429-434 "read 1233 us, write 1856 us" per GetInputFocus pass). Since 2026-09-20 the transport is XLITE-RING (memfd rings + eventfd doorbells, xlite/xring.h:1-40; current-state.md:100-102) and no ring round-trip time is recorded anywhere (grep: none). So the per-warp cost is somewhere between ~1 ms and ~6 ms - a 5x band - and the "15-19%" could equally be 60%+, at which point the client cannot drain motion events between frames and the model (one warp per event, events queue, several round trips per frame) changes entirely.

2. Event rate is not 125 Hz to the client under load. lvdesk emits motion to a grabbed client from mouse_poll() (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9196, the grab block at :9440-9476), called on every poll wake where a mouse fd is readable (lvdesk.c:10485) - the "~125 Hz" is lvdesk's own comment (lvdesk.c:10256-10258). But all reports drained in one wake collapse to ONE xshim_pointer (rx/ry vs g_x/g_y, :9470-9473), and xshim folds motion still sitting in an unflushed output buffer (lvdesk/xshim.c:3117-3137). With Quake saturating the CPU, how often lvdesk gets to run decides the client-visible rate, and that has never been counted. The route also omits that each warp currently produces TWO extra events the client must read and discard: the synthetic centre MotionNotify (xshim.c:7287-7296) and, on lvdesk's next wake, a duplicate centre motion because xwin_on_warp resets ptr_x/ptr_y (lvdesk.c:5074-5087) while g_x/g_y still hold the old position (:9470). Unmeasured either way; per the brief, an unmeasured assumption under the expected fps defaults to refuted.

3. A step in the route would make the mouse DEAD, so the effort is understated: "XIQueryDevice/XIFreeDeviceInfo stubs". SDL2's XI_RawMotion handler calls xinput2_get_device_info -> X11_XIQueryDevice (Buildroot sdl2-2.32.10 src/video/x11/SDL_x11xinput2.c:235) and returns 0 ("oh well") when it gets NULL (:289-292); the valuator classes' mode selects relative vs absolute deltas (:246-253). XIQueryDevice must be a real libXi-format reply with two XIValuatorClass entries in XIModeRelative, not a stub.

4. The stock libXi cannot deliver the events on xlite; the cookie path is hand-written or nothing. libXi.so.6.1.0 is on the target (58,568 bytes, target usr/lib), and xlite has the request primitives stock extension libs use (_XGetRequest/_XReply, xlite/xlite_int.c:109, :217; XextAddDisplay, xlite/xlite_req.c:2511), so XIQueryVersion/XISelectEvents may work as-is. But libXi registers its wire-to-cookie decoder through XESetWireToEventCookie, which xlite stubs to return NULL (xlite/xlite_ext.c:22-42), and XGetEventData/XFreeEventData are generated stubs (no XLITE_IMPL anywhere; only in xlite/libX11-exports.txt:175,196). xlite's event decoder is 32-byte fixed (xlite/xlite.c:128, :198; only replies carry a length, :586-587), so GenericEvent length handling, the FP3232 valuator decode and the cookie fill are all new xlite code. The route's "or provide the cookie fill directly" is the only path, not an alternative.

5. Double count. R3 (TyrQuake's own in_x11 backend) removes the same round trip: in_x11.c IN_CenterMouse is XSelectInput + XWarpPointer + XSelectInput with no XSync/XFlush (tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/in_x11.c:89-96; grep XSync/XFlush in in_x11.c: none). R7 concedes it is moot if R3 ships, so it cannot be counted alongside it.

6. Prior record: nothing on XI2 or the warp storm was measured or rejected (grep XInput/XI2/warp in docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md: none). The only recorded warp-adjacent cost is hit_test at ~1% CPU at 125 Hz motion, xshim side (docs/x11-review.md:94-96). The 2026-09-24 entry records only that tyr-quake traces "motion + recentring warps + cursor hide" (perf-plan:313-315) - presence, not a rate.

7. Mechanism confirmed, for the record: TyrQuake 0.71 uses SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode (common/in_sdl.c:65, :584-586); X11_SetRelativeMouseMode returns SDL_Unsupported without XI2 (SDL_x11mouse.c:381-384); SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode falls back to relative_mode_warp (src/events/SDL_mouse.c:1142-1153); SDL_PrivateSendMouseMotion then calls WarpMouse on every non-centre motion (SDL_mouse.c:558-576); WarpMouseInternal is XWarpPointer + X11_XSync (SDL_x11mouse.c:319-358). With XI2 at >= 2.0, XI_RawMotion feeds SDL_SendMouseMotion(relative=1) with no warp (SDL_x11xinput2.c:274-320). Answer 2.0 exactly: 2.2 makes SDL select XI_Motion per window and deactivates MotionNotify (SDL_x11xinput2.c:333-335, :450).

What survives: the route's own cheapest test (one boot, timedemo A/B/A with and without uinject drag, XSHIM_PROF counts of op 41 and op 43, xshim.c:2777-2790 keyed at :9622) is the right first step and costs no code; it should include a ring round-trip time, which is the missing number. Nothing in R7 should be built before that count exists.

result.reasoning:
Verified from source (repo root /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux). The route does not break a rule, but its expected fps rests on two things it did not read and one stale number, and the family it re-enters was already closed.

1. THE WAIT IT ADDS IS A BUSY-SPIN, NOT A BLOCK. vid_x.c:1049-1052 waits for ShmCompletion with `while (!oktodraw) VID_ProcessEvents();`, and VID_ProcessEvents (vid_x.c:931-939) is `while (XPending(x_disp)) XNextEvent(...)`. In xlite, XPending -> XEventsQueued(QueuedAfterFlush) (xlite.c:1080-1081), which is deliberately NON-BLOCKING (xlite.c:1060-1078: "pump() blocks ... wedges XPending() ... xclock never ticked again") and does one `poll(fd,0)` per call (xlite_read_more, xlite.c:498-506). A measured af_unix poll here is 0.15 ms (memory s31-socket-syscalls-cost-ms, XSHIM_PROF). So for the whole window from flush to event delivery - the xshim copy+hash (>=3.09 ms for 153,600 B quiet, accel-plan.md:35; 11.98 ms loaded) plus the wake-ups - the client hammers poll() on CPU0, the same CPU lvdesk/xshim present on (perf-plan C45: moving the 3.6 ms present off CPU0 is forbidden). ~20 x 0.15 ms = ~3 ms of client CPU per frame that the SDL2 path does not spend: SDL2 blocks in recvmsg inside XSync (SDL_x11framebuffer.c:183,219 = XShmPutImage + X11_XSync; xlite XSync -> xlite_reply, xlite.c:1018-1046). The route's arithmetic books "wait for ShmCompletion (xshim copy >=3.09 ms + ~1 ms wake)" as if it were free and books "removes SDL2's per-pump poll()" as a win - both inverted: the X11 target keeps VID_ProcessEvents' XPending per frame (vid_x.c:1078) AND adds the spin. The gross saving (one 153,600 B SDL_BlitCopy, 3.09-4.0 ms at the ~38 MB/s memcpy rate xshim.c documents) is roughly cancelled by the spin. Net is 0 +/- ~3%, unmeasured.

2. STEPS 1-2 AS WRITTEN HANG, so "correct by construction" is not established. xlite's XShmPutImage hardcodes `r[30] = 0; /* sendEvent: no completion */` (xlite_req.c:2856) and ignores its send_event argument (2831 `(void)send_event`), so xshim never sees the byte the route keys on. Independently, XShmPutImage deliberately does not flush (xlite_req.c:2864-2880) and XEventsQueued does not flush either (xlite.c:1050-1078), so the put sits in the client's output buffer while the client spins on XPending forever - exactly the hang the route's own cheapest_test names. Two further xlite changes (pass sendEvent through; flush in XEventsQueued/QueuedAfterFlush or in the put) are needed and unbudgeted. XSynchronize is indeed a no-op (xlite_req.c:1919-1924) and every X call vid_x.c/in_x11.c/x11_core.c make exists in xlite except XShmGetEventBase and the five XF86VidMode* (checked against XLITE_IMPL/symbols.txt) - those parts of the evidence hold.

3. STALE BASELINE. The 10.7 fps / 93.8 ms figure predates the lean alsa.conf ship: perf-plan-2026-09-23.md log 2026-09-24 records stock 0.71 at 11025/-mem 10 = 12.4 fps (1,595 majflt), 48 kHz/-mem 20 = 8.5; menu.conf's timedemo line runs `-window` (overlay/etc/lvdesk/menu.conf:28), so the VidMode/fullscreen step is not on the path to the goal number. The post-ship profile shows all memcpy at 4% and VID_Update at 2.9% of samples, which caps the SDL_BlitCopy saving at <=~3.2 ms of an 80.6 ms frame (<=4%) BEFORE the spin cost - so even the gross ceiling is below the route's +3-5% and inside the +/-10% per-boot lottery.

4. ALREADY CLOSED FAMILY. perf-review-2026-09-23.md:162-168 (T2.4, "the last X round trip") bounds the whole ShmCompletion/XSync family at <=2.5% Quake, and perf-plan:98-101,720-723 closed it: XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT (now shipped, xlite.c:1008-1016) deleted the wait outright and moved the canary -5% inside an 11% A-to-A gap - "nothing cheaper than deleting the wait can be worth more". R4 goes the other way: it ADDS a second round trip per frame (ShmCompletion wait then XSync, vid_x.c:1049-1056) on top of the one SDL2 has. No prior measurement of the X11 target itself exists (grep vid_x/VID_TARGET/Xxf86vm in both docs: none), so it is not a repeat, but its present-path lever is the closed one.

Not a double-count with other levers per se, but its gross gain overlaps X2-11 (drop the pre-reply copy) territory already recorded as ~0 in fullscreen.

Rule check (rule_ok=true): VID_TARGET/IN_TARGET/SND_TARGET are stock Makefile variables (Makefile:105-124, 934-940, 970-972, 1016-1023); the shipped build already passes non-defaults (USE_SDL=Y, CD_TARGET=null, rootfs/build-tyrquake.sh), so a build-target choice is "its own build system", not app config steering. Note the Linux default is SND_TARGET=pulseaudio (Makefile:128-130), so "the stock Linux default" is only true for video/input. The libXxf86vm shim is ours (precedent xlite/randr), not a library substituted into the app's own code, and is not needed for the windowed timedemo. Audio path and SD placement unchanged.
